42970643.bottom_line: In 1857 patients after successful left atrial appendage closure, both a reduced-dose NOAC for 3 months and aspirin alone were noninferior to 6 months of DAPT for the 6-month composite of death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding, with less bleeding on either monotherapy.
42970643.design: Open-label, 3-group, multicenter randomized noninferiority trial at 87 US investigational sites, with 1:1:1 allocation; randomization October 2024 to December 2025 and final 6-month follow-up in July 2026. Noninferiority was tested in the primary analysis population with a 1-sided Farrington-Manning test (alpha = .025).
42970643.population: 1857 patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation who had undergone successful left atrial appendage closure and were eligible for all 3 regimens. Mean age 76 (SD, 8) years, 42.9% female, mean CHA2DS2-VASc score 4.2 (SD, 1.3), and 68.0% with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
42970643.intervention: Reduced-dose non-vitamin K oral anticoagulant (NOAC) for 3 months followed by aspirin (n = 620), or aspirin alone for 12 months (n = 613).
42970643.comparison: Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for 6 months followed by aspirin (n = 624).
42970643.outcomes: Primary outcome was the 6-month composite of all-cause death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding: 41 patients (6.9%) with DAPT vs 31 (5.1%) with reduced-dose NOAC (risk ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.48-1.18]; risk difference, -1.7 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, 1.2) and 20 (3.3%) with aspirin alone (risk ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.29-0.82]; risk difference, -3.5 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, -0.8). Both monotherapy strategies met noninferiority criteria (P < .001 for noninferiority for both). The noninferiority margin was not reported.
key_results: Primary composite at 6 months: 6.9% (41/624) with DAPT, 5.1% (31/620) with reduced-dose NOAC, 3.3% (20/613) with aspirin alone.
Reduced-dose NOAC vs DAPT: risk ratio 0.75 (95% CI, 0.48-1.18); risk difference -1.7 percentage points, 97.5% upper bound 1.2; noninferiority met (P < .001).
Aspirin alone vs DAPT: risk ratio 0.49 (95% CI, 0.29-0.82); risk difference -3.5 percentage points, 97.5% upper bound -0.8; noninferiority met (P < .001).
Major bleeding (exploratory, no multiplicity adjustment): 4.5% with DAPT, 2.7% with reduced-dose NOAC, 1.7% with aspirin alone.
Clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (exploratory): 8.7% with DAPT, 4.8% with reduced-dose NOAC, 3.8% with aspirin alone.
Device-related thrombus at 45 days (exploratory): 3.4% with DAPT, 0.9% with reduced-dose NOAC, 2.7% with aspirin alone.
strengths: Randomized three-group comparison that directly addresses a common post-procedural question for which no adequately powered randomized data previously existed.
Large sample (1857 patients) across 87 US sites in a typical older, high-stroke-risk LAAC population (mean CHA2DS2-VASc 4.2), supporting generalizability to US practice.
Clinically relevant composite primary endpoint combining thrombotic and bleeding harms, so a regimen cannot look good simply by trading one for the other.
Prespecified noninferiority testing with a 1-sided Farrington-Manning test at alpha = .025, and the aspirin-alone arm met noninferiority with a risk difference upper bound below zero.
limitations: Open-label design, so management and ascertainment of bleeding events could be influenced by knowledge of treatment assignment; whether endpoint adjudication was blinded is not reported.
Follow-up for the primary endpoint was only 6 months, while the aspirin-alone arm continued to 12 months; longer-term stroke and device-related thrombus outcomes are not reported.
Bleeding and 45-day device-related thrombus rates were exploratory and not adjusted for multiplicity, so the apparent bleeding advantage of monotherapy is hypothesis-generating.

Enrollment was restricted to patients with uncomplicated, successful closure who were eligible for all 3 regimens, so results do not apply to complicated implants or patients with a specific indication for anticoagulation.
Device-related thrombus was numerically highest with DAPT (3.4%) and lowest with reduced-dose NOAC (0.9%) but the comparison was exploratory and event numbers were not reported.
The specific NOACs, doses used, and trial funding source are not reported in the abstract.
42970643.practice_implications: After uncomplicated left atrial appendage closure in patients eligible for any regimen, 6 months of DAPT no longer looks necessary: aspirin alone, or a reduced-dose NOAC for 3 months followed by aspirin, gave noninferior 6-month composite outcomes with numerically less major and nonmajor bleeding. Aspirin alone is the simplest option and had the lowest primary event rate, though its 2.7% device-related thrombus rate versus 0.9% with reduced-dose NOAC is worth weighing in patients judged at higher thrombotic risk, and these exploratory signals plus the 6-month horizon argue for individualized choice pending longer follow-up.

candidates.title: Ventricular Fibrillation During Pulsed Field Ablation With Dual-Energy Focal Catheters in Patients With Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arrhythmia induction during catheter ablation in patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) has been reported, but the risk associated with pulsed field ablation (PFA) remains poorly characterized.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the procedural incidence of unexpected ventricular fibrillation (VF) during PFA in patients with CIEDs and describe associated clinical and device findings.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study of consecutive PFA procedures in patients with CIEDs. All procedures were reviewed for unexpected VF.
RESULTS: Among 107 consecutive procedures using PFA energy in patients with CIEDs, 83 were atrial and 24 were ventricular ablations. Unexpected VF occurred in 4 patients (overall incidence 3.7%, 95% CI 1.0% - 9.3%): 1 during left atrial PFA for pulmonary vein isolation and 3 during left ventricular PFA for ventricular tachycardia ablations. VF occurred at ablation sites both near and remote from CIED lead tips. Device electrograms demonstrated prominent ablation artifact with abnormal triggered activity and mode switch behavior. Intra-procedural recordings also demonstrated local capture and R on T mechanisms.
CONCLUSIONS: Unexpected VF during PFA in patients with CIEDs occurred in 3.7% of procedures. These results complement prior adverse-event reports and support systematic pre-, intra-, and post-procedure CIED management, with external defibrillation immediately available, whenever PFA or dual-energy ablation is performed in patients with cardiac devices.

candidates.title: Surgical outcomes of infective endocarditis in children and adults with congenital heart disease.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Reports describing surgery for infective endocarditis (IE) in children and adults with congenital heart disease (CHD) are limited. This study aimed to determine the patient characteristics, preoperative conditions, surgical outcomes, and risk factors in this cohort.
METHODS: All children and adults with CHD who underwent surgical treatment for IE between 2001 and 2024 were reviewed. Patient characteristics and surgical procedures were evaluated; survival, recurrent IE, and risk factors were analyzed.
RESULTS: A total of 96 patients underwent surgical treatment for IE, including 52 children and 44 adults with CHD. Underlying CHD included ventricular septal defect in 31 patients, aortic stenosis/insufficiency in 26, and tetralogy of Fallot in 14. The most frequently infected lesion was the aortic valve in 40 patients, and the most frequently detected organism was Staphylococcus species in 34 patients. Vegetation was observed in 65 patients. Median age at surgery was 17.2 (IQR: 11.7-29.4) years. In-hospital mortality was 6.3%, and survival at 5, 10, and 20 years was 90.6, 88.1, and 80.5%, respectively. Freedom from recurrent IE was 96.4% at 20 years. Number of previous operations (hazard ratio (HR): 1.585, p=0.005), gram-negative bacteria (HR: 11.475, p<0.001), emergency operations (HR: 17.988, p=0.001), and longer aortic cross-clamp time (HR: 1.011, p=0.043) were risk factors for mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: In children and adults with CHD, mortality following surgery for IE was low, and recurrent IE was rare. Individualized management based on the patient's preoperative condition and the causative organism appears to be important for improving survival.

candidates.title: Aortic Root Abscess in Infective Endocarditis: Prognostic Impact and Outcomes of Patch Repair.
candidates.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Due to discrepancies between guidelines and expert consensus, we examined the perioperative and mid-term outcomes of aortic root abscesses to determine their prognostic significance and optimal surgical management.
METHODS: We completed a single-center retrospective study of patients surgically treated for aortic valve infective endocarditis (AV IE) from 2019 to 2024. We compared outcomes in patients with and without root abscess, and among abscess cases, between patch repair and extended surgery (root reconstruction or replacement). The primary outcome was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE, composite of all-cause death, heart failure (HF) readmission, and stroke). Outcomes were analyzed using Kaplan Meier estimators and Cox proportional hazards.
RESULTS: Among 158 patients (57% with abscess) with a median follow-up of 1.22 years (IQR 0.13-2.53), root abscesses were associated with increased MACCE (adjusted HR 3.15 (1.51-6.59), p=0.002) and HF readmission (SHR 4.54 (1.55-13.30), p=0.006). In patients with aortic root abscess, 62 underwent patch repair and 21 underwent extended surgery. Patch repair was associated with decreased MACCE (adjusted HR 0.34 (0.15-0.74), p=0.006), all-cause mortality (p=0.002), and death at 30 days (13% vs 33%, p=0.035) compared to extended surgery.
CONCLUSIONS: Aortic root abscess was associated with increased MACCE and HF readmissions compared to AV IE without abscess, identifying root abscess as a marker of adverse prognosis and supporting prompt recognition and referral in aortic valve endocarditis. Patch repair for aortic root abscesses is a safe and reasonable approach in patients with suitable anatomy compared to more extensive surgery.

candidates.title: Digital Health Intervention to Optimize Heart Failure Management After Hospital Discharge in Brazil (OPT-HF): A Randomized Clinical Trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Barriers to optimizing guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for heart failure include infrequent clinical visits, clinician inertia, and poor patient knowledge. Digital health interventions (DHIs) may mitigate these barriers, but evidence from low- and middle-income countries is limited. We evaluated whether a DHI would improve GDMT use and other outcomes in Brazil.
METHODS: We enrolled adults admitted for heart failure with ejection fraction <50% and GDMT gaps (≥1 GDMT class not started or ≥2 classes ≤50% target dose) across 5 Brazilian public hospitals from November 2023 to August 2025. Participants were randomized to usual care or the DHI comprising a patient-facing app linked to a provider dashboard, supporting nurse-led remote monitoring, cardiologist teleconsultations, and self-care education. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in mean heart failure GDMT score (0-12) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included differences in health status, self-care, hospitalization rates, and all-cause mortality. Intention-to-treat analyses used baseline-adjusted linear regression and estimated risk ratios.
RESULTS: Among 154 randomized patients (DHI: 87; usual care: 67), mean age was 65±14 years; 62% were male, 66% were Black, 44% had ≤4 years of education, and 68% were New York Heart Association class III/IV. Primary outcome data were available for 141 participants (91.6%; DHI: 81; usual care: 60). Mean GDMT scores increased from 7.2 in both groups to 10.5 with DHI versus 7.5 with usual care at 90 days (changes: +3.3 versus +0.3 points; adjusted difference, 3.01 [95% CI, 2.30-3.73]; P<0.001). A borderline difference was observed in health status (7.89; P=0.052). Improvements were observed in self-care (β=14.79 [95% CI, 9.78-19.81]; P<0.001). Fewer participants were hospitalized with DHI than usual care (9/87 [10.3%] versus 15/67 [22.4%]; risk ratio, 0.46 [95% CI, 0.21-0.99]; P=0.048), with no statistically significant difference for deaths.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients hospitalized for heart failure in Brazil, a context-adapted DHI improved GDMT use, self-care, and reduced hospitalizations. These findings provide early randomized evidence supporting DHI for GDMT optimization in low-resource settings.

candidates.title: Electrocardiographic and Echocardiographic Markers of Atrial and Ventricular Remodeling Allow Identification of Cardiac Sarcoidosis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac sarcoidosis (CS) is a rare but life-threatening manifestation of systemic sarcoidosis. Although positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging provide high diagnostic accuracy, they are unsuitable for first-line screening. Widely available modalities such as electrocardiography (ECG) and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) focusing only on ventricular abnormalities show limited sensitivity.
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate whether a combined diagnostic model integrating ECG and TTE parameters, emphasizing atrial and ventricular remodeling, can accurately identify patients with CS.
METHODS: We prospectively included 252 consecutive patients with biopsy-proven sarcoidosis. CS was defined by characteristic findings on PET-CT or cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. A comprehensive set of atrial and ventricular ECG and TTE parameters was analyzed. Diagnostic models were constructed using univariable and multivariable logistic regression, and discriminative performance was assessed.
RESULTS: CS was identified in 37 (14.7%) patients. On ECG, prolonged P-wave duration, prolonged QRS duration, and reduced T-wave amplitude in lead aVR were independently associated with CS. On TTE, increased left atrial volume index, increased left ventricular end-diastolic diameter, and impaired left ventricular global longitudinal strain emerged as significant predictors. ECG- and TTE-based models showed comparable discrimination for CS identification (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve: 0.87 for both). A combined ECG/TTE model, driven primarily by QRS duration, left atrial volume index, and left ventricular global longitudinal strain, achieved the highest diagnostic performance (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve: 0.90).
CONCLUSIONS: An exploratory multimodal, noninvasive approach integrating atrial and ventricular ECG and TTE markers provides high diagnostic accuracy for identifying CS and may serve as a pragmatic screening and triage tool to guide referral for advanced cardiac imaging. candidates.title: Conduction System Pacing in Pediatric Patients: Outcomes From a Multicenter International Cohort.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) may be advantageous in children requiring lifelong ventricular pacing, but long-term durability data are limited.
OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to evaluate the long-term preservation, durability, and safety of CSP in pediatric patients.
METHODS: This international, multicenter, retrospective study included consecutive patients aged ≤18 years undergoing His bundle pacing or left bundle branch area pacing at 9 experienced centers. The primary endpoint was long-term preservation of CSP.
RESULTS: Among 120 patients (mean age 12.6 ± 3.7 years), 68 (56.7%) had congenital atrioventricular block, 41 (34.2%) had congenital heart disease, and 12 (10.0%) underwent CSP for heart failure/cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). Acute CSP implantation, defined as achievement of His bundle pacing, left bundle branch pacing, or left ventricular septal pacing, was successful in 116 patients (96.7%). After a median follow-up of 24 months (Q1-Q3: 10-54 months), electrical lead performance remained stable. Among 101 patients with CSP at implantation and follow-up capture assessment, CSP was preserved in 95 (94.1%). Kaplan-Meier-estimated freedom from loss of CSP was 100.0% at 1 year and 98.2% (95% CI: 94.7%-100.0%) at 2 and 3 years. CSP lead-related complications occurred in 10 patients (8.3%), and reintervention was required in 9 (7.5%). In the CRT subgroup, left ventricular ejection fraction improved from 28.8% ± 9.4% to 46.8% ± 12.0% (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: CSP is a feasible, safe, and durable physiological pacing strategy in children, with excellent long-term CSP preservation and stable electrical performance despite ongoing somatic growth. CSP may also provide effective physiological resynchronization in pediatric patients requiring CRT.

candidates.title: Characteristics and Thresholds of Coronary Lesions to Predict Acute Coronary Syndrome From Artificial Intelligence-Guided Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Characteristics of future culprit lesions according to artificial intelligence-guided quantitative computed tomography (AI-QCT) are unknown.
OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to characterize and derive thresholds to predict future culprit lesions from coronary computed tomography angiography using AI-QCT.
METHODS: A total of 2,169 patients/13,772 lesions undergoing coronary computed tomography angiography at Turku University Hospital, Finland, (derivation) and 553 patients/3,948 lesions from Amsterdam University Medical Center, the Netherlands, (validation) were analyzed with AI-QCT. Lesions from vessels undergoing early revascularization were excluded. Lesion-level total plaque volume (TPV) and noncalcified plaque volume (NCPV) thresholds were derived and externally validated to predict lesion-level and patient-level acute coronary syndrome (ACS).
RESULTS: Future culprit lesions from both cohorts (n = 69 validation; n = 15 derivation) had consistently higher median TPV (101 mm3 validation; 115 mm3 derivation; P = 0.811) and NCPV (65 mm3 validation; 74 mm3 derivation; P = 0.709) compared with control lesions (P < 0.001) and were nonobstructive in 69.6% (derivation) and 40.0% (validation). Thresholds of TPV ≥55 mm3 and NCPV ≥32 mm3 were derived and associated with significantly higher adjusted rates of lesion-level (TPV ≥55 mm3: adjusted HR: 12.09; 95% CI: 6.95-21.04; P < 0.001; NCPV ≥32 mm3: adjusted HR: 10.82; 95% CI: 6.22-18.80; P < 0.001) and patient-level ACS (TPV ≥55 mm3: adjusted HR: 2.92; 95% CI: 1.65-5.16; P < 0.001; NCPV ≥32 mm3: adjusted HR: 5.11; 95% CI: 2.49-10.46; P < 0.001) with consistent results in the validation cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: Future culprit lesions vs nonculprit lesions by AI-QCT demonstrated significantly higher plaque volumes and were nonobstructive in 40% to 70%. Thresholds of TPV ≥55 mm3 and NCPV ≥32 mm3 were derived to predict future culprit lesions and associated with increased rates of lesion-level and patient-level ACS in 2 independent cohorts.

candidates.title: CT-Based Deep Learning Assessment of Aortic Valve Fibrosis and Calcification: Development and Multicenter External Validation Against Experts, Histology, and Outcomes.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Computed tomography angiography (CTA) enables assessment of aortic valve tissue composition, providing insights into disease progression and helping predict outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis (AS). The authors aimed to develop a deep learning system for CTA-based quantification of aortic fibrotic and calcific tissue, validate its agreement with expert manual analysis and histopathology, and evaluate its value for outcome prediction.
METHODS: This international, multicenter study included 1,674 patients who underwent CTA at 9 sites. A deep learning model based on the nnU-Net architecture was trained in 468 patients and applied to an external test set of 1,206 patients, including 29 with valve histology and 12 with serial CTA. In 1,165 patients with clinical outcomes, prognostic value was assessed adjusting for clinical, echocardiographic, and procedural covariates.
RESULTS: Deep learning-enabled tissue composition analysis was rapid (1.35 ± 0.4 min vs 7.2 ± 1.2 min for experts) with excellent agreement vs expert assessment (r = 0.915; intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] = 0.913), histology (r = 0.909; ICC = 0.905), and scan-rescan reproducibility (r = 0.999; ICC = 0.999). In the external cohort, 469 patients (40%) died over 4.1 ± 1.1 years of follow-up. Fibrotic tissue volume (adjusted HR [aHR] 1.42 per IQR increase; P < 0.001), calcific tissue attenuation (aHR 1.02 per 25 HU increase; P = 0.005), left ventricular ejection fraction (aHR 1.10 per 5% decrease; P < 0.001), life-threatening bleeding (aHR: 1.96; P = 0.003), major vascular complication (aHR: 1.51; P = 0.042) and postprocedural peak pressure gradient (aHR 1.03 per 1 mm Hg increase; P < 0.001) independently predicted mortality. Patients in the highest tertile of fibrotic tissue volume (>0.940 cm3) had a 2-fold higher risk of death (aHR: 2.0; P < 0.001), whereas patients with dense calcific tissue attenuation (>885 HU) had a 1.5-fold higher risk of death.
CONCLUSIONS: Deep learning enables rapid quantification of aortic valve fibrotic and calcific tissue from CTA, demonstrating excellent agreement with both expert CTA and histological assessments. Quantitative analysis of aortic tissue composition provides additional prognostic value for all-cause mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in multicenter external evaluation.

candidates.title: Ventricular arrhythmia-heart failure interaction and mortality in ICD recipients after myocardial infarction.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: Ventricular arrhythmia (VA) and heart failure (HF) frequently coexist in patients with ischaemic left ventricular (LV) dysfunction. Whether VA and HF events are bidirectionally associated remains unclear. We investigated their bidirectional relationship and associations with mortality.
METHODS: We analysed 1014 patients from the multicentre WICD-MI study. All received a wearable cardioverter-defibrillator after acute myocardial infarction (MI) and subsequently underwent implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) implantation, with persistent LV ejection fraction ≤35%. Associations between ICD-treated VA, HF-events (HF hospitalization, heart transplantation, or LV assist device implantation), and all-cause mortality were assessed using time-dependent Cox models.
RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 2.6 years post-ICD implantation, VA was independently associated with an increased risk of HF events [aHR = 3.50 (1.66-7.38), P = .001], while HF events similarly preceded subsequent VA [aHR = 2.96 (1.59-5.50), P = .0008]. Both were independently associated with all-cause mortality, with a numerically higher aHR for HF events [aHR = 7.96 (4.71-13.47), P < .0001] than for VA [aHR = 4.43 (2.35-8.36), P < .0001]. Sensitivity analyses suggested that the VA-HF association was strongest for shock-treated arrhythmias. In exploratory analyses, VA was strongly associated with subsequent HF events in subcutaneous ICD recipients [aHR = 15.08 (4.62-49.22), P < .0001] but not in transvenous ICD recipients (P for interaction = .0002).
CONCLUSION: In ICD recipients with persistent LV dysfunction following MI, VA and HF events are bidirectionally associated and independently associated with mortality. The VA-HF association was strongest for shock-treated arrhythmias. These findings highlight the potential value of integrated HF and VA management.

candidates.title: The Art Behind the Algorithm: Hybrid Ablation and the Need for a Lifetime Strategy in Non-Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation.
candidates.abstract: The management of persistent and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation remains highly variable in clinical practice, despite increasingly refined guidelines and an expanding ablation armamentarium. Treatment sequencing is frequently driven by local program infrastructure and institutional culture, and hybrid ablation is often deferred until multiple endocardial procedures have failed, by which point progressive atrial remodeling may have already narrowed the therapeutic window. Randomized and registry data support a meaningful role for hybrid ablation earlier in the disease course of selected patients with non-paroxysmal AF, particularly those with enlarged atria, prolonged AF duration, advanced substrate, or failed prior endocardial ablation. Contemporary pulsed-field ablation technology has improved procedural safety and efficiency, yet freedom from recurrence at one year in persistent AF remains substantially lower than in paroxysmal AF across all current energy platforms, reflecting the complexity of atrial substrate over time. This ongoing myocardial remodeling places non-paroxysmal AF closer to a chronic structural cardiac disease than to a discrete procedural target and demands a lifetime management strategy rather than a sequence of isolated procedural decisions. The mindset for other progressive structural cardiac diseases has already moved in this direction-aortic valve stenosis is now managed through a multidisciplinary team that integrates anatomy, timing, procedural durability, and long-term risk across the full patient trajectory. We propose an AF Heart Team framework for non-paroxysmal AF in which catheter-based, hybrid, and surgical strategies are selected according to disease phenotype and lifetime trajectory, with the goal of intervening before advanced remodeling reduces the likelihood of durable rhythm control.

candidates.title: Normative Values for QRS Duration in Athletes aged 12-35 years undergoing Pre-participation Exams.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Due to limited data on athletic QRS duration, this cross-sectional study aims to establish normative digital reference values in asymptomatic, apparently healthy athletes ages 12 to 35 undergoing pre-participation examinations.
OBJECTIVES: We hypothesized that QRS duration of athletes would be longer in males, increase with age, and rarely exceed 120 ms in the absence of a bundle branch block.
METHODS: We analyzed QRS duration from standardized digital ECG recordings in 9,084 athletes (58% male, age 12-35 years, mean age 18) obtained during pre-participation examinations. Sex-stratified 99th-percentile quantile-regression equations were developed and applied in an APP to demonstrate that QRS duration outliers could be easily identified.
RESULTS: Females had shorter QRS durations than males (88.5 +/- 8.3 ms vs. 97.3 +/- 9.1 ms; mean difference 8.9 ms, 95% CI: 8.5-9.2 ms). QRS duration demonstrated a positive cross-sectional association with age and was greater in men than women. Female 97.5th and 99th percentile QRS duration were 106.0 ms and 108.0 ms, respectively, with range 62-130 ms. Male 97.5th and 99th percentile QRS duration were 116.0 ms and 118.3 ms, respectively, with range 70-132 ms. 7(0.2%) females and 55 (1.0%) males had QRS duration >120 ms. 99th percentile quantile regression equations were derived (Female: QRS=99.6 + 0.56 x age; Male: QRS = 104.7 + 0.74 x age).
CONCLUSIONS: Our results indicate that defining prolonged QRS criteria necessitates adjustments according to age and sex. To facilitate future prospective research, we offer specific regression models to detect outliers.

candidates.title: Coronary angiography in heart transplants from donors older than 40: a Eurotransplant study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The increasing age of heart donors in Europe raises concerns about undetected coronary artery disease (CAD), a contributor to early graft dysfunction and long-term complications. This study examined the association between donor coronary angiography (CA) and heart transplant utilization, particularly in donors aged >40 years.
METHODS: A total of 20 681 donor heart offers reported to Eurotransplant between 2004 and 2020 were analysed. The use of CA, donor characteristics, and acceptance rates were assessed. CAD status was imputed for donors without angiography using logistic regression based on clinical risk factors. Transplantation probabilities were modelled using observed and imputed CAD severity to explore potential differences under a scenario of broader CA availability.
RESULTS: CA was performed in 23.5% of cases, predominantly in older donors and those with cardiovascular risk factors. Among donors with CA, 37.5% had CAD, which was significantly associated with age, male sex, hypertension, and smoking. Donors with normal CA findings had lower odds of rejection compared with those without CA (odds ratio 0.36, P < .0001). In a counterfactual model, broader CA availability in donors aged >40 years was associated with a higher estimated transplant utilization (56.4%-67.1%), corresponding to a model-based increase of ∼535 transplants.
CONCLUSIONS: In this observational cohort, CA availability was associated with differences in donor heart utilization, particularly when findings were normal or showed non-significant CAD. These findings suggest that angiographic information may reduce diagnostic uncertainty and support clinical decision-making in older donors. A risk-adapted, resource-sensitive approach to CA use is warranted.

candidates.title: Efficacy of empagliflozin in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction according to the presence of echocardiographic features of diastolic dysfunction in the EMPEROR-Preserved trial.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: To define the impact of diastolic dysfunction (DD) on the response to empagliflozin treatment in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Diastolic dysfunction was defined by left atrial volume index ≥34 ml/m2, the ratio of early diastolic mitral inflow velocity to early diastolic mitral annular tissue velocity (E/e) ≥ 13 or left ventricular mass index >115 (males) or >95 (females). We created three categories of increasing DD (0, 1, or ≥2 DD criteria at baseline) to describe the effect of DD on response to empagliflozin therapy and adverse effects. Of 5988 patients in the EMPEROR-Preserved trial, 3766 (63%) had no documented baseline DD, 1619 (27%) had one, and 603 (10%) had two or more measures. Baseline DD was associated with sex, race, ethnicity, and region and was more common with lower heart rate, DBP, body weight, and eGFR. Despite baseline DD not being significantly associated with the primary endpoint of hospitalization for heart failure or cardiovascular death within the placebo group, a progressive treatment effect across the three DD categories was seen (trend test P-value .0014), with estimated hazard ratios of empagliflozin vs placebo of 0.91 (none present), 0.64 (1 present), and 0.49 (≥2). A significant treatment-by-subgroup trend test was also observed for the total number of hospitalizations for heart failure. Both Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score improvement at week 52 and safety profile were consistent across DD categories.
CONCLUSION: Baseline detection of echocardiographic DD predicted improved clinical response to empagliflozin in a graded fashion, but the reasons cannot be reliably determined from this analysis.

candidates.title: Pacing Performance of a Modular Communicative Leadless Pacing-Defibrillator System.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: MODULAR ATP is an ongoing trial assessing the efficacy of a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter defibrillator (S-ICD) in communication with a leadless pacemaker (LP) that can deliver bradycardia pacing and antitachycardia pacing. The objective of this study was to assess safety and pacing performance of the investigational LP.
METHODS: The study enrolled patients with an ICD indication and at high risk for monomorphic ventricular tachycardia. Pacemaker dependent patients were excluded. Primary safety endpoint 2 was the percentage of patients free from major LP-related complications at 12 months. The secondary effectiveness endpoint assessed the rate response performance of the LP under workload. Parameters related to the pacing performance were also measured.
RESULTS: In 297 patients, the mean age was 59±12 years, the mean left ventricular ejection fraction was 35.3±13.1%, and 17.5% were female. LP implant was attempted in 286 patients and was successful in 100%. The major LP-related complication free rate at 12 months was 97.2% (one-sided 97.5% LCL 94.5%), surpassing the performance goal of 81%. There were no LP-related complications following Implant. For the secondary effectiveness endpoint, the slope of the normalized sensor rate versus the normalized workload was 0.96 (95% LCL 0.91, 95% UCL 1.02), within the performance goal range of 0.65-1.35. At 12 months, 96.8% of patients had a pacing capture threshold ≤ 2V @ 0.4ms pulse width.
CONCLUSIONS: The performance of the modular pacing-defibrillator system at one year demonstrated a low complication rate and reliable pacing functionality.

candidates.title: Impact of Infarct Type on Serious Arrhythmic Event Detection and Cardiovascular Outcomes During Telemedical Monitoring After Myocardial Infarction: A SMART-MI substudy.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with LVEF 36-50% and cardiac autonomic dysfunction remain at risk after myocardial infarction (MI) despite not qualifying for primary-preventive defibrillator therapy. Implantable cardiac monitor (ICM)-based telemonitoring facilitates early detection of serious arrhythmic events (SArE), however it remains unclear whether infarct type modifies the detection and prognostic significance of SArE.
OBJECTIVE: To compare the effect of ICM monitoring on SArE detection by infarct type and explore associations with subsequent major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE).
METHODS: SMART-MI randomized MI survivors with LVEF 36-50% and cardiac autonomic dysfunction to ICM-based telemonitoring or conventional follow-up. Cox models assessed effects on SArE detection and treatment-by-infarct-type interaction. Exploratory analyses modeled detected SArE as a time-dependent covariate, stratified by arm, for subsequent MACCE.
RESULTS: 400 patients were randomized to ICM implantation (n=201, 122 STEMI) or conventional follow-up (n=199, 114 STEMI). Telemedical monitoring increased SArE detection in STEMI (HR 11.99, 95% CI 3.67-39.17) and NSTEMI (HR 4.44, 95% CI 2.09-9.43; both p<0.001). Although the effect was numerically greater in STEMI, clinically relevant effect modification cannot be excluded (p for interaction=0.154). Detected SArE were associated with subsequent MACCE in both, STEMI and NSTEMI with HR of 7.77 (95% CI 3.20-18.86) and 4.26 (95% CI 1.44-12.58), respectively.
CONCLUSION: ICM-based telemonitoring increased SArE detection in both STEMI and NSTEMI patients and detected SArE were associated with subsequent MACCE in both infarct types. These findings support further investigation of intensified rhythm-surveillance strategies in high-risk STEMI and NSTEMI patients.

candidates.title: Local Conformal Auditing Exposes and Restores Reliability of AI-ECG Atrial Fibrillation Detection Under External Deployment Shift.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: AI-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) can detect atrial fibrillation (AF), but safe deployment depends on calibration, subgroup reliability, and explicit error guarantees, not on discrimination alone.
OBJECTIVE: To test whether the conformal-prediction coverage guarantee of an AF ECG classifier survives external deployment shift, and whether a small local labeled audit restores it without retraining.
METHODS: A four-class 12-lead rhythm classifier trained on PTB-XL (Germany; 7,831 ECGs, 7,164 patients) was evaluated unchanged on Chinese (Chapman-Shaoxing; n=2,289) and US (Georgia; n=1,990) cohorts. We measured discrimination, expected calibration error (ECE), 90%-target split-conformal coverage, subgroup coverage, label-free shift corrections, local recalibration across audit sizes, and an AF auto-clear policy with finite-sample risk control.
RESULTS: AF AUC remained 0.998 (95% CI 0.997-0.999) in China but fell to 0.936 (0.919-0.952) in the US cohort. ECE rose from 0.051 to 0.197 and 0.237, and source-calibrated coverage fell from 0.901 to 0.758 and 0.722 (both P<0.001). Coverage was lower in Chinese men than women (0.707 vs 0.822; difference 0.115, 95% CI 0.081-0.148). Label-free corrections failed. Local recalibration restored mean coverage to 0.90 with 50 labeled ECGs but with wide variability (95% simulation interval 0.82-0.97), narrowing to 0.86-0.94 at 200 ECGs. Local AF risk control certified auto-clearing of 68% of held-out ECGs in China but abstained in the US cohort.
CONCLUSION: AI-ECG uncertainty can fail silently despite high AUC. A local conformal audit detects when uncertainty estimates are untrustworthy and recalibrates the uncertainty layer without changing the classifier, converting trust into a measurable, subgroup-aware, task-specific guarantee.

candidates.title: Characteristics and Mechanisms of Septal Myocardial Injury and Repair Following Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) requires screwing the lead deep into the interventricular septum. Multiple attempts are often required to achieve proper capture of the conduction system.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of deep screwing attempts on septal myocardial injury and repair and to explore the underlying mechanisms.
METHODS: Prospective LBBAP implantation was performed in 41 patients with bradycardia. Serum creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB) and left ventricular (LV) global longitudinal strain (GLS) were used to evaluate myocardial damage. Mechanisms of septal damage were explored in 24 LBBAP canines using histopathological and molecular changes.
RESULTS: Compared to patients with ≤ 3 attempts, those with >3 attempts had a higher incidence of CK-MB elevation (6 vs. 44%, P=0.004), a less negative LV endocardial (-17.9 vs. -13.6 %, P<0.001), and mid-myocardial GLS (-15.3 vs. -12.4 %, P<0.001). In animal study, molecular changes associated with >3 attempts featured amplified HMGB1-centered sterile inflammation and enhanced CD206+ macrophage-mediated profibrotic remodeling. Canines with >3 attempts were characterized by three markedly thickened concentric reparative layers around the lead-inner thrombus layer, middle fibrous sheath layer, and outer reactive fibrotic layer. Interestingly, removal of the pacing lead after >3 attempts resulted in only mild scattered fibrosis, with markedly attenuated CD206+ macrophage-mediated profibrotic pathway.
CONCLUSIONS: LBBAP with >3 deep septal screwing attempts was associated with a higher risk of septal myocardial injury and markedly thickened concentric reparative layers, underpinned by more pronounced sterile inflammation, profibrotic remodeling, and foreign body reaction.

candidates.title: Reproductive factors in women with familial hypercholesterolaemia.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: Hypercholesterolaemia has been associated with earlier menarche and menopause; however, these observations may reflect reverse causation or confounding. Familial Hypercholesterolaemia (FH) provides a model to investigate these associations. This study compared reproductive characteristics and pregnancy outcomes in women with FH vs. women without FH.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Between November 2023 and April 2025, women with FH aged ≥40 years were recruited from two university hospital outpatient clinics in the Netherlands and Norway. Women without FH were selected from the Rotterdam Study and Norwegian population-based cohorts. FH cases were matched 1:2 to women without FH on age, smoking status, body mass index, and ethnicity using nearest-neighbour matching. Information on reproductive factors and pregnancy outcomes were obtained via an online survey. 484 women with FH and 968 matched women without FH (median age 55 years [IQR 48-62]; 93% North-Western European) were included. Cardiovascular disease prevalence was higher in women with FH (22% vs. 4%; P < 0.001). Most women with FH (95%) used lipid-lowering therapy, LDL cholesterol levels were lower compared to controls (2.5 vs. 3.5 mmol/L; P < 0.001). Women with FH more often had been pregnant (91% vs. 84%; P < 0.001). Prevalence of gestational diabetes (4% vs. 4%; P = 0.70) and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (16% vs. 13%; P = 0.10) was similar; however, preeclampsia was more frequent in FH (11% vs. 7%; P = 0.030). Age at menarche (13.2 vs. 13.1 years; P = 0.43), age at menopause (50 years; P = 0.92), and reproductive lifespan (36 years; P = 0.98) were similar between groups.
CONCLUSION: Reproductive lifespan is comparable between women with and without FH, but FH was associated with a higher prevalence of preeclampsia, highlighting the importance of targeted pregnancy monitoring and prevention.

candidates.title: Plozasiran for Severe Hypertriglyceridemia and Risk of Pancreatitis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe hypertriglyceridemia is associated with an increased risk of acute pancreatitis. Plozasiran, a small interfering RNA targeting APOC3 messenger RNA, lowers triglyceride levels and potentially mitigates the risk of acute pancreatitis.
METHODS: In two double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, 757 adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive plozasiran (25 mg) or placebo at baseline and at months 3, 6, and 9. These trials had identical designs, end points, and analytic plans. The primary end point was the percent change in the fasting plasma triglyceride level from baseline to month 12. Key secondary end points were the percent change in the fasting triglyceride level from baseline to month 10, a fasting triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter (5.6 mmol per liter) and less than 150 mg per deciliter (1.7 mmol per liter), the percent change in the fasting serum triglyceride level at month 12 for patients with a baseline triglyceride level of 880 mg per deciliter or greater, and changes in remnant cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol. A pooled analysis addressed adjudicated acute pancreatitis, incidence, and first-event timing.
RESULTS: At month 12, patients in the plozasiran groups had a median triglyceride level that was lower than the baseline level by 79% and 81% in the two trials. These reductions corresponded to a median difference in the plozasiran groups as compared with the placebo groups (placebo-adjusted change) of -45 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -51 to -38) and -47 percentage points (95% CI, -54 to -39). A triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter at 12 months was reported in 91% and 93% of the patients in the plozasiran groups and in 51% and 50% of those in the placebo groups (P<0.001). The rates of acute pancreatitis were 1 per 100 patient-years with plozasiran and 5 per 100 patient-years with placebo (rate ratio, 0.22; P = 0.008). Adverse events during treatment occurred in 73% of the patients in both the pooled plozasiran and placebo groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia, the use of plozasiran resulted in lower triglyceride levels and a lower risk of acute pancreatitis than placebo at 12 months. (Funded by Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals; SHASTA-3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06347003; SHASTA-4, NCT06347016.).

candidates.title: Obesity, frail obesity, and outcomes after durable left ventricular assist device implantation: a pooled analysis of the MOMENTUM 3 trials.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Obesity in patients supported by left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) is linked to excess mortality and haemocompatibility-related events. Whether this association persists with the fully magnetically levitated HeartMate 3 (HM3) pump is unknown. This analysis tested outcomes with obesity and the additive influence of co-existing frailty ('frail obesity') in the contemporary era.
METHODS: The study pooled 2200 HM3 recipients from the MOMENTUM 3 pivotal randomized trial (n = 515) and Continued Access Protocol (n = 1685). Obesity was defined as body mass index (BMI) ≥30 kg/m2 and frailty by a 40-item Rockwood cumulative-deficit frailty index (FI), with clinically relevant frailty defined as FI ≥0.325 (moderate-severe frailty); BMI was excluded from the FI to avoid mathematical coupling. The primary endpoint was survival to transplant, recovery, or 24 months of support free of disabling stroke (modified Rankin score >3) or pump replacement reoperation.
RESULTS: Obese patients (n = 887, 40.3%) were younger, less often with ischaemic aetiology, and more frequently women, but more often had diabetes and hypertension, than non-obese patients. Unadjusted 2-year outcomes were similar between groups (freedom from the primary endpoint: 75.1% vs 77.1%, log-rank P = .34; survival: 79.9% vs 81.2%, P = .57). After covariate adjustment, obesity was independently associated with a higher risk of the primary endpoint (hazard ratio [HR] 1.30, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.07-1.58) and all-cause mortality (HR 1.35, 95% CI 1.10-1.67), as well as heart failure hospitalization, infection, and arrhythmia, but not stroke, bleeding, or early right heart failure. Frailty affected 67.3% of obese recipients (571/849) and was associated with a higher adjusted risk of the primary endpoint (HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.09-2.10), overall mortality and non-haemocompatibilty-related morbidity endpoints. The obesity-by-frailty interaction was not significant for either the primary endpoint (P = .436) or mortality (P = .215), indicating additive rather than synergistic risk; frail-obese patients nonetheless carried the highest absolute risk of any subgroup. Frailty improved by at least one severity class by 6 months in 75.9% of frail-obese patients, and improvement was associated with better survival (adjusted HR 0.14, 95% CI 0.07-0.26).
CONCLUSIONS: In the HM3 era, obese and non-obese recipients had similar unadjusted 2-year outcomes; however, after adjustment for baseline case-mix, obesity was independently associated with a higher risk of both the primary endpoint and all-cause mortality, together with heart failure hospitalization, infection, and arrhythmia. Frailty was independently associated with adverse outcomes across nearly all endpoints and was highly prevalent among obese recipients; the combination of obesity and frailty was additive but not synergistic, with frail-obese patients carrying the highest absolute risk. Frailty, however, proved substantially reversible after LVAD support, and its improvement was associated with markedly better survival. Obesity and frailty should therefore be assessed together, rather than through BMI thresholds alone, with recognition that frailty status is dynamic after implantation and that improvement in frailty is associated with markedly better survival.

candidates.title: A randomized comparison of comprehensive weight loss intervention vs. usual care on recurrences of atrial fibrillation in obese patients after catheter ablation: HOBIT-AF trial.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: Obesity is one of the strongest risk factors for the development of atrial fibrillation (AF), and its reduction is associated with the alleviation of AF burden. The HOBIT-AF study aimed to evaluate the impact of complex weight loss interventions on AF recurrence rate in obese individuals after catheter ablation (CA).
METHODS AND RESULTS: The HOBIT-AF was a randomized controlled trial with a 15-month treatment period (3-18 months post CA) involving complex weight-reducing interventions in the active arm. The primary outcome was the change in AF/atrial tachycardia (AT) burden assessed from baseline and the final 14-day Holter monitoring. A total of 167 individuals (aged 59 years, body mass index of 35.6 kg/m2) were randomized into the active (n = 85) and control group (n = 82). At the end of the treatment period, a mean reduction of 6.8 ± 7.0% of the initial body weight accompanied by improvement of metabolic parameters was achieved in the active group. The AF/AT burden change was 0.6 ± 2.5% (95% CI: -4.2-5.5%) in the active group and -0.9 ± 1.8% (95% CI: -4.5-3.0%) in the control group. The AF/AT recurrence-free survival during the 3-18-month follow-up period was comparable between groups (70.4% vs. 69.6%).
CONCLUSION: HOBIT-AF trial showed that despite the beneficial effect of body weight reduction on metabolic profile of obese patients with predominantly paroxysmal AF after CA, no reduction in AF/AT recurrence was observed in comparison with control patients. This may be likely due to low AF burden after previous CA, limiting further improvement.

candidates.title: Single vs Double ProGlide Devices for Access Site Closure after Transfemoral Aortic Valve Replacement: The SINGLE-CLOSURE Trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite advances in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), access-site vascular complications remain an important source of procedural morbidity. The conventional double-ProGlide strategy may increase the risk of access-site stenosis and other vascular complications, particularly in patients with challenging iliofemoral anatomy. Retrospective studies have suggested that a single-ProGlide strategy may offer an effective alternative, but this strategy has not yet been evaluated in a randomized trial.
OBJECTIVES: This trial aimed to determine whether a single-ProGlide strategy could offer a simpler alternative to the conventional double-ProGlide strategy without increasing vascular complications.
METHODS: The SINGLE-CLOSURE trial was a prospective, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 25 centers in China. Patients aged ≥65 years scheduled for transfemoral TAVR were assigned 1:1 to single-ProGlide or double-ProGlide closure for the main access site. The primary endpoint was the in-hospital composite of Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-3-defined access-site or access-related major and minor vascular complications.
RESULTS: A total of 876 patients were randomized. In the modified intention-to-treat population, the primary endpoint occurred in 57 of 436 patients (13.1%) in the single-ProGlide group and 65 of 430 patients (15.1%) in the double-ProGlide group, meeting the prespecified criterion for noninferiority (risk difference: -2.2%; 95%: -7.0% to 2.6%; P = 0.013; noninferiority margin: 3.19%). Access-related major vascular complications occurred in 2 patients (0.5%) in the single-ProGlide group and 6 patients (1.4%) in the double-ProGlide group. Among the secondary endpoints, individual components of the primary endpoint, access-related bleeding, time to hemostasis, and all-cause mortality were similar between groups. Access-site stenosis was numerically less frequent with the single-ProGlide strategy (5.0% vs 7.9%), whereas additional closure devices might be used more often (2.5% vs 0.9%).
CONCLUSIONS: A single-ProGlide strategy was noninferior to conventional double-ProGlide closure for the composite of VARC-3-defined access-site or access-related vascular complications after transfemoral TAVR. Primary endpoint events were predominantly minor vascular complications.

candidates.title: Percutaneous Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Symptomatic Mitral Regurgitation: 2-Year Outcomes From the ENCIRCLE Trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) is an approved treatment option for select high-risk patients with symptomatic mitral regurgitation (MR). The main cohort of the ENCIRCLE trial, evaluating fully percutaneous transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system, demonstrated 13.9% mortality, significant MR reduction, and improved functional and health status outcomes at 1 year.
OBJECTIVES: We report 2-year outcomes from the main cohort of the ENCIRCLE trial.
METHODS: Eligible symptomatic patients with ≥3+ MR who were not suitable for surgery or transcatheter edge-to-edge repair underwent TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system. Independent study oversight included an echocardiographic core laboratory and a clinical events committee. Endpoints included the nonhierarchical composite rate of all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization (HFH) as well as clinical, echocardiographic, functional, and health status outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 299 patients were treated, with 2-year follow-up data available for 202 of 210 eligible patients (96.2%). Mean age was 75.5 ± 9.3 years, 50.8% were men, and the mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score for mitral valve replacement was 6.6% ± 4.1%. At 2 years, MR reduction was sustained, with MR ≤1+ in 97.0% patients (P < 0.001). The 2-year composite rate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 35.6% (25.1% all-cause mortality, 23.0% HFH). In a 365-day landmark analysis, 1- to 2-year rates were 13.0% for all-cause mortality and 10.6% for first HFH. At 2 years, the rates of disabling stroke, clinically significant valve thrombosis, and hemolysis requiring intervention were 6.6%, 7.1%, and 7.6%, respectively. There were no instances of clinically significant left ventricular outflow obstruction. Improvements in functional and health status outcomes were sustained with 87.0% of patients in NYHA functional class I/II (P < 0.001) and a mean Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire overall summary score increase of 17.2 points (P < 0.001). The 6-minute walk distance increased by +9.0 ± 97.3 m compared to baseline (P = 0.246).
CONCLUSIONS: The 2-year results of the ENCIRCLE trial demonstrated durable near MR elimination with sustained improvements in functional and health status outcomes in surviving patients. These findings support transseptal TMVR as a therapeutic option for carefully selected patients with symptomatic MR. (The ENCIRCLE Trial [ENCIRCLE]; NCT04153292).

candidates.title: Defining the Substrate in Scar-Related Ventricular Tachycardia: A Hierarchy of Evidence for Arrhythmogenicity.
candidates.abstract: Scar-related monomorphic ventricular tachycardia is sustained by a limited re-entry circuit within a much larger field of diseased myocardium. Late gadolinium enhancement cardiac magnetic resonance and cardiac computed tomography define scar distribution, channel architecture, wall thickness, and tissue composition, but cannot demonstrate conduction or circuit participation. Voltage mapping and abnormal electrograms identify electrically abnormal myocardium, although their appearance depends on activation sequence, catheter geometry, contact, and annotation. Functional mapping reveals rate-dependent slowing, decrement, and block that may be concealed during baseline rhythm. Mapping during ventricular tachycardia (VT) provides the most direct evidence of circuit participation, but is often limited by hemodynamic instability, noninducibility, or incomplete surface representation of a 3-dimensional circuit. This review examines how to weight these findings when defining the arrhythmogenic substrate. Structural imaging establishes where a circuit could reside and how it may be accessed. Baseline electroanatomic mapping characterizes the electrical expression of surviving myocardium, while functional mapping tests whether conduction deteriorates with changes in wave front or coupling interval. Activation and entrainment provide the strongest evidence that a region participates in a specific VT. These findings should be integrated hierarchically rather than by simple spatial overlap, adjusting interpretation for disease phenotype, substrate depth, mapped surface, and recording conditions. The arrhythmogenic substrate is best understood as surviving myocardium within scar whose 3-dimensional architecture and electrophysiological behavior permit re-entry. A reproducible definition will require standardized acquisition and annotation, explicit reporting of the evidence linking a region to VT, and prospective validation using mapped circuits.

candidates.title: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate in chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: the H-HeFT trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate (H-ISDN) has shown benefit in earlier randomized trials of patients with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and chronic heart failure. This trial tested if H-ISDN could reduce worsening heart failure or mortality in patients with chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) receiving contemporary treatment.
METHODS: The Hydralazine-Isosorbide Dinitrate in Patients With Chronic Heart Failure Trial (H-HeFT) was a multicentre, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in patients with HFrEF at 23 Danish hospitals (New York Heart Association class II-IV, elevated N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and LVEF ≤40%). Target treatment was hydralazine 75 mg/isosorbide dinitrate 40 mg three times a day (t.i.d). The primary endpoint was a composite of hospitalization with worsening heart failure, an urgent outpatient visit resulting in intravenous/metolazone therapy for heart failure, heart transplantation, left ventricular assist device implantation, or death. Secondary endpoints included components of the primary outcome.
RESULTS: Overall, 592 predominantly White patients (median age 72 years, 18% women) were randomized with a mean follow-up of 3.7 years. The primary outcome occurred in 90 of 294 patients (30.6%) in the H-ISDN group and in 91 of 298 patients (30.5%) in the placebo group [hazard ratio (HR) 0.90; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.67-1.21; P = .48]. There were 57 deaths in the H-ISDN group vs 72 in the placebo group (HR 0.72; 95% CI 0.51-1.02); worsening heart failure events occurred in 52 vs 47 patients (HR 1.01; 95% CI 0.68-1.50).
CONCLUSIONS: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate did not change the incidence of the composite endpoint of heart failure events or death in patients with heart failure and LVEF ≤40%.

candidates.title: Long-term Prognostic Value of Sequential Coronary CT Angiography and Quantitative PET in Suspected Chronic Coronary Syndromes: A Multicentre study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The long-term prognostic value of a guideline-recommended selective sequential anatomical-functional imaging strategy using coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) followed by quantitative [15O]H2O positron emission tomography (PET) remains uncertain. We evaluated its long-term prognostic value in patients with first symptoms suggestive of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD).
METHODS: In this multicentre European cohort, symptomatic patients first underwent CCTA and were selectively referred to quantitative [15O]H2O PET in case of suspected obstructive stenosis (≥50%). Patients were stratified according to CCTA findings and PET-derived ischaemia (normal CCTA; non-obstructive CAD on CCTA; obstructive CAD on CCTA without ischaemia; obstructive CAD on CCTA with ischaemia). The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), and hospitalization for unstable angina (UA). Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) were calculated.
RESULTS: Among 3,918 patients (61.0±9.8 years; 54.3% female) with a median follow-up of 5.1 [3.8-8.0] years, 278 (7.1%) experienced the primary endpoint. aHRs increased stepwise across CCTA-PET categories. Compared to normal CCTA, non-obstructive CAD and obstructive CAD without ischaemia were associated with a higher risk of the combined primary endpoint (aHR 1.89, [95%CI: 1.23-2.91], p=0.004; aHR 3.20, [95%CI: 1.95-5.25], p<0.001). Among patients with obstructive CAD on CCTA, PET-derived ischaemia further increased the risk of the primary endpoint (aHR 1.55, [95%CI: 1.05-2.30]; p=0.029), but not when excluding UA from the composite endpoint (aHR 1.37, [95%CI 0.90-2.07]; p=0.141). PET-derived ischaemia primarily predicted events within the first year, while obstructive CCTA findings remained associated with long-term hard outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: A sequential strategy combining CCTA and quantitative [15O]H2O PET provides robust and incremental long-term risk stratification. While PET-derived ischaemia refines prediction of short-term and symptom-driven events, CCTA-derived CAD remains the principal determinant of long-term hard outcomes.

candidates.title: Sex-based differences in the atrial fibrillation care pathway and outcomes: an ITHACA-database analysis.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: To characterize sex-specific differences in clinical presentation, evaluate progression through the atrial fibrillation (AF) care pathway from diagnosis to catheter ablation (CA) and assess long-term outcomes.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This was a retrospective cohort study of patients with incident AF at Northwell Health between 2015 and 2024 from the ITHACA-database. Sex-specific differences in clinical presentation were examined. The AF care pathway was operationalized as a stepwise cascade, modelling conditional drop-off to identify care gaps. Sex-specific CA risk ratios were assessed via Poisson regression. Incident AF was identified among 165 563/655 459 patients (71.4 ± 11.6 years, 32% non-white, 45% female) with a recorded diagnosis of AF. Women were older (73.3 ± 10.6 vs. 69.8 ± 12.1 years, P < 0.001), had higher rates of dementia (9.1% vs. 5.2%), stroke (8.6% vs. 7.4%) and congestive heart failure (21.5% vs. 20.8%) at diagnosis. Transfer-of-care gaps [median 3.6 years follow-up, 96% retention] were identified at every level: 31.5% of women vs. 35.3% of men were evaluated by cardiology, 16.2% vs. 21.6% by electrophysiology, and 3.5% vs. 5.7% underwent CA (all P < 0.001). Women were 16% less likely to receive CA (RR 0.84 95% CI 0.77-0.91). In cause-specific Cox models, female sex was associated with incident stroke (aHR 1.24, 95% CI 1.18-1.30) and dementia (aHR 1.30, 95% CI 1.24-1.35), but modestly lower mortality after adjustment (aHR 0.96, 95% CI 0.94-0.99).
CONCLUSION: In this real-world analysis, significant sex-specific differences in clinical phenotype at presentation, progression through the AF care pathway and clinical outcomes were observed.

candidates.title: Long-term outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stents versus coronary artery bypass grafting for left main coronary artery disease: a prospective analysis of the multicentre IRIS-MAIN registry.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with drug-eluting stents has been widely used to treat patients with left main coronary artery disease; however, long-term comparative outcomes versus coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in real-world populations remain poorly characterised. We aimed to compare long-term all-cause mortality after PCI or CABG in Asian patients with unprotected left main coronary artery disease.
METHODS: We analysed prospectively collected data from the multicentre IRIS-MAIN registry, conducted at 46 hospitals in South Korea, India, Japan, Indonesia, and Malaysia. The registry enrolled adults aged 18 years or older with unprotected left main coronary artery disease (defined as a stenosis diameter of ≥50% as visually estimated on angiography), who had been treated with PCI, CABG, or medical therapy alone. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. We used a target trial emulation framework to compare the long-term risk of all-cause mortality between PCI with drug-eluting stents and isolated CABG. We used propensity-score overlap weighting to adjust for measured baseline covariates. The IRIS-MAIN Registry study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01341327).
FINDINGS: Between Jan 1, 2003, and Dec 31, 2024, 6900 patients were enrolled in the IRIS-MAIN registry, of whom 5379 (78·0%) underwent coronary revascularisation through either PCI with drug-eluting stents (3836 [71·3%]) or CABG (1543 [28·7%]) and were included in the analysis. The median duration of follow-up for all patients was 10·0 years (IQR 5·0-16·7). In the overlap-weighted population, no statistically detectable difference in 10-year weighted Kaplan-Meier rates of all-cause mortality was observed between PCI and CABG (24·0% vs 22·9%; overlap-weighted hazard ratio 1·00 [95% CI 0·87-1·14]; p=0·99). The confidence interval does not exclude a mortality benefit or harm with either strategy.
INTERPRETATION: In this non-randomised registry analysis of patients with left main coronary artery disease, there was no statistically detectable difference in all-cause mortality between PCI and CABG. For patients considered suitable for either strategy, multidisciplinary Heart Team discussion might help patients and clinicians weigh potential trade-offs in the choice between PCI and CABG. These findings are observational and cannot establish causal treatment effects or equivalence in survival.
FUNDING: The CardioVascular Research Foundation (South Korea).

candidates.title: Efficacy and Safety of Routine Postdilation in Balloon-Expandable Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Platform: The DUOTAP Randomized Clinical Trial.
candidates.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: In patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), asymmetric valve expansion can estimate prosthetic dysfunction and death. Postdilation has shown promising results in optimizing valve geometry in observational studies; however, randomized evidence is currently lacking.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the efficacy of routine postdilation on transcatheter heart valve (THV) geometry and hemodynamic performance, and associated safety outcomes.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: DUOTAP was a single-center, single-blinded randomized clinical trial. Recruitment took place from January 2025 to April 2026 and end points were assessed periprocedurally (fluoroscopy) at 30 days (adverse events) and at 3 months (computed tomography [CT]). The trial was conducted at a high-volume tertiary referral center, the Medical University of Vienna, Austria. Included patients had severe AS suitable for transfemoral TAVI with a balloon-expandable THV and without high-risk features on preprocedural CT or coronary angiography and were randomized in a 1:1 ratio, stratified by THV size, to routine postdilation vs no postdilation. These data were analyzed from July 2026 to September 2026.
INTERVENTION: Routine postdilation using the original delivery balloon at the identical filling volume. A sham procedure was performed in the control group.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The fluoroscopic THV asymmetry index served as primary end point. Further fluoroscopic and CT-derived measures of valve geometry, hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT), paravalvular leak (PVL), and THV hemodynamics on echocardiography, and freedom from major procedural adverse events served as secondary end points.
RESULTS: Overall, 148 patients (median [IQR] age, 81 [77-85] years; 69 female [46.6%] and 79 male [53.4%]; median EuroSCORE-II, 2.3%) underwent randomization (n = 74 intervention vs n = 74 control). Intervention yielded a 70% lower THV asymmetry index compared with control (median: 1.2% vs 2.8%; geometric mean ratio: 0.30; 95% CI, 0.18-0.47; P < .001), with consistent effects across prespecified subgroups, induced by frame height reduction across the outer curve. Additionally, intervention yielded numerically larger THV diameters on fluoroscopy and significantly larger THV areas at the inflow, midframe, and outflow level on CT. HALT and mild or worse PVL were significantly less frequent and the Doppler Velocity Index was significantly higher in the intervention group. No differences in procedure-related adverse events between groups were recorded (χ2 test: P = .36).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, postdilation led to reduced THV asymmetry, optimized geometry, and improved hemodynamic performance, without increasing procedure-related adverse events. These results support the use of routine postdilation to optimize THV geometry and hemodynamics in suitable patients.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07477002.

candidates.title: Prognostic value of Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio after percutaneous coronary intervention.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) physiological indices have prognostic relevance. Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (μQFR) enables wire-free, rapid, single-view functional assessment, yet its long-term prognostic value after PCI remains incompletely established.
AIMS: We sought to evaluate the prognostic value of post-PCI μQFR for long-term adverse outcomes.
METHODS: This prespecified subgroup analysis of the FAVOR III China trial included 3,825 patients. All PCI-treated vessels with a reference diameter ≥2.5 mm and 50-90% diameter stenosis were analysed for offline post-PCI μQFR. The primary endpoint was 5-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; including death from any cause, myocardial infarction, or ischaemia-driven revascularisation).
RESULTS: Post-PCI μQFR was successfully analysed in 4,196 vessels from 3,455 patients, with similar distributions between the randomised treatment groups. At 5 years, a low post-PCI μQFR was associated with a higher incidence of MACE compared with the intermediate and high post-PCI μQFR tertiles (23.1% vs 19.0% vs 17.2%; p=0.001). Using the highest tertile (μQFR>0.95) as a reference, adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) were 1.08 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.87-1.34) for the intermediate tertile (0.92-0.95) and 1.30 (95% CI: 1.06-1.60) for the lowest tertile (μQFR ≤0.91). Using a receiver operating characteristic-derived cutoff, MACE occurred more frequently in patients with post-PCI μQFR <0.94 (22.3% vs 17.4%, aHR 1.23, 95% CI: 1.04-1.47; p=0.02) than in those with post-PCI μQFR ≥0.94. No significant interaction was observed between treatment strategy and post-PCI μQFR (p for interaction=0.23).
CONCLUSIONS: Post-PCI μQFR distributions were similar between treatment groups, but lower values were associated with higher 5-year adverse event risk without significant treatment interaction. Its limited binary discrimination supports use as a continuous metric for post-PCI physiological risk stratification. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT03656848).

candidates.title: Prediction of coronary events by computed tomography-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (CT-μFR) provides a non-invasive measure of vessel-level ischaemia but may not capture local haemodynamic abnormalities reflected by the longitudinal pressure gradient across the lesion (CT-μFR gradient).
AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the association of CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient with 3-year vessel-level subsequent coronary events and to determine the incremental prognostic value of their combined assessment.
METHODS: Our study included a total of 885 vessels from 312 patients who underwent invasive coronary angiography for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or stable angina and had prior CCTA performed 6 months to 3 years earlier. CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient were assessed by an independent core laboratory blinded to the clinical data. The primary outcome was 3-year subsequent coronary events (a composite of vessel-specific myocardial infarction or urgent revascularisation for ACS). The discrimination ability of predictive models was assessed using Harrell's C-index.
RESULTS: Vessels with CT-μFR ≤0.80 or a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm had a higher risk of events than those with CT-μFR>0.80 (79.1% vs 20.4%, adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 6.87, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.26-8.96; p<0.001) or a CT-μFR gradient <0.004/mm (72.6% vs 27.4%, adjusted HR 4.08, 95% CI: 3.15-5.28; p<0.001), respectively. Among vessels with CT-μFR>0.80, a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm remained associated with increased risk (adjusted HR 2.59, 95% CI: 1.63-4.11; p<0.001). Adding the CT-μFR gradient to CT-μFR improved discrimination in the overall cohort (C-index 0.700 to 0.755; p<0.001) as well as the subgroup with CT-μFR>0.80 (C-index 0.575 to 0.655; p<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Both CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient are independently associated with 3-year subsequent coronary events. Their combined assessment improves risk stratification beyond CT-μFR alone. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04794868).

candidates.title: A randomised non-inferiority trial of CCTA guidance versus IVUS guidance for PCI: rationale and design of the P4 clinical trial.
candidates.abstract: Intravascular imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves clinical outcomes compared with angiography-guided PCI. Contemporary coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides comprehensive assessment of coronary anatomy, plaque characteristics, vessel dimensions, calcification, and lesion-specific physiology, enabling detailed procedural planning before catheterisation. The Precise Procedural and PCI Plan (P4) trial is a prospective, international, multicentre, randomised, open-label trial with blinded endpoint adjudication designed to determine whether a comprehensive CCTA-guided PCI strategy is non-inferior to intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided PCI with respect to clinical outcomes. Approximately 1,100 patients with chronic coronary syndromes or stabilised acute coronary syndrome, at least one coronary stenosis >70%, and fractional flow reserve derived from CCTA ≤0.80 are enrolled. Following central core laboratory confirmation of anatomical and physiological eligibility, patients are randomised 1:1 to CCTA-guided or IVUS-guided PCI. Patients assigned to CCTA-guided PCI undergo standardised procedural planning and virtual PCI simulation, with CCTA integrated into the catheterisation laboratory using computed tomography-fluoroscopy synchronisation for intraprocedural guidance. In the IVUS-guided arm, PCI is performed with mandatory pre- and post-PCI IVUS assessment. The primary endpoint is target vessel failure at 12 months, defined as the composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction, or ischaemia-driven target vessel revascularisation. P4 will determine whether comprehensive, non-invasive CCTA-guided PCI planning is non-inferior to IVUS-guided PCI regarding 12-month target vessel failure while potentially improving procedural efficiency and standardisation. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05253677).
