candidates.title: Prediction of Bailout Mechanical Circulatory Support Use for Hemodynamic Collapse During PCI: The ORACLE Score.
candidates.abstract: Background: Bailout mechanical circulatory support (MCS) may be used in the setting of intraprocedural hemodynamic collapse during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). We developed and externally validated a simple risk prediction model for bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse during PCI. Methods: Consecutive patients undergoing PCI at a tertiary hospital between 2018 and 2025 were included in the derivation cohort (n=6,931), after excluding cases of salvage PCI and procedures performed with pre-existing or prophylactic MCS. The primary endpoint was bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse. A multivariable Firth logistic regression model was developed, internally validated, and translated into a simplified integer-based risk score (ORACLE). External validation was performed in 214,877 PCIs from the Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan Cardiovascular Consortium (BMC2) registry. Results: The incidence of bailout MCS was 1.4% in the derivation cohort. Six variables (non-elective presentation, systolic blood pressure, chronic heart failure, prior PCI, rotational/orbital atherectomy, and left main PCI) independently predicted the primary endpoint. The regression model demonstrated good discrimination both in the derivation (area under the curve [AUC] 0.817; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.774-0.860) and external validation (AUC 0.761; 95% CI 0.753-0.770) cohorts. The simplified ORACLE score preserved most of the discriminatory performance of the full model (AUC 0.791 in the derivation cohort and 0.718 in the external validation cohort) and effectively stratified patients, with observed bailout MCS rates ranging from 0.4% in the low-risk category to 8.7% in the high-risk group, with similar findings in the external validation cohort. Discrimination was consistent across clinically relevant subgroups. Negative predictive value was >99% in both the derivation and external validation cohorts. Conclusions:: ORACLE is a simple score to estimate the risk of bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse during PCI, which may support preprocedural risk assessment.

candidates.title: Accuracy of Virtual Circle Method and Valve-to-Aorta Distance Change After Redo-TAVR: Multicenter Paired CT Analysis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The virtual circle method is currently used in preprocedural computed tomography planning for Redo-transcatheter aortic valve (TAV) replacement to simulate the predicted outer boundary of the index TAV and the valve-to-aorta distance for coronary risk assessment, yet its accuracy against postprocedural observations has not been evaluated. This study aimed to assess the accuracy of the virtual circle method in predicting index TAV expansion and coronary risk following a second TAV implantation using paired preprocedural and postprocedural computed tomography in patients undergoing Redo-TAV replacement.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 58 patients who underwent Redo-TAV replacement at 5 sites with paired preprocedural and postprocedural cardiac computed tomography. Three valve combinations were analyzed: Evolut-in-SAPIEN (n=17), SAPIEN-in-SAPIEN (n=13), and SAPIEN-in-Evolut (n=28). Index TAV frame expansion was quantified by area- or perimeter-derived diameter change. Accuracy of the virtual circle method was defined as a diameter difference within ±1 mm between predicted and observed index TAV frame diameter.
RESULTS: In the Evolut-in-SAPIEN combination, meaningful index SAPIEN frame expansion occurred only with effective pre/postdilatation, whereas in both the SAPIEN-in-SAPIEN and SAPIEN-in-Evolut combinations, consistent frame expansion was observed regardless of dilatation. Changes in index frame diameter corresponded inversely to changes in valve-to-aorta distance. In the SAPIEN-in-Evolut combination, expansion was governed chiefly by implant position and sizing strategy. Across all combinations in which the virtual circle method was applicable (n=53), accurate prediction was achieved in 31 patients (58.5%), with overestimation in 14 (26.4%) and underestimation in 8 (15.1%).
CONCLUSIONS: The virtual circle method provided an accurate or conservative (overestimating) estimate of index TAV expansion and coronary risk in the majority of patients (85%), supporting its clinical utility for Redo-TAVR planning. The remaining 15% showed underestimation of modest magnitude (median, 1.3 mm), occurring predominantly in patients who underwent predilatation and postdilatation, warranting heightened caution in borderline coronary anatomy when dilatation strategies are employed.

candidates.title: 3-Year Comparison of Sirolimus- Versus Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Femoropopliteal Artery Disease: The SIRONA Trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sirolimus-coated balloons (SCBs) have emerged as alternatives to paclitaxel-coated balloons (PCBs), but randomized comparative data beyond 2 years are lacking.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare patient-reported outcomes, effectiveness, and safety through 3 years in symptomatic femoropopliteal artery disease.
METHODS: SIRONA was a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial comparing SCB angioplasty with a PCB strategy. Patients were randomized 1:1 after successful predilation. Prespecified 3-year outcomes included walking capacity, health-related quality of life, clinically driven target lesion/vessel revascularization (cdTLR/cdTVR), mortality, major amputation, and amputation-free survival.
RESULTS: Among 482 randomized patients (SCB, n = 238; PCB, n = 244), 96.3% had intermittent claudication; 3-year follow-up was completed by 76.5% and 79.6%, respectively. Changes in patient-reported walking distances did not differ between-groups. Three-year freedom from cdTLR was 88.2% (95% CI: 83.1%-91.9%) versus 80.2% (95% CI: 74.1%-85.0%; HR: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.36-0.97; nominal log-rank P = 0.03). Post-hoc analysis suggested time-varying treatment effects (treatment-by-period interaction P = 0.006), with separation after the first year. Freedom from cdTVR (HR: 0.78, 95% CI: 0.50-1.21; nominal P = 0.27) and amputation-free survival (HR: 1.09, 95% CI 0.57-2.09; nominal P = 0.79) did not differ.
CONCLUSIONS: Through 3 years, no between-group differences were observed in walking capacity and health-related quality of life or clinical safety outcomes between SCB angioplasty and the PCB strategy. Three-year freedom from cdTLR was higher with SCB angioplasty, with treatment effect that varied over time. Given the exploratory, nonmultiplicity-adjusted 3-year analysis, the cdTLR difference requires confirmation.

candidates.title: The interplay of fibrinogen and lipoprotein(a) with 20-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk: a path analysis within the ATTICA study (2002-2022).
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: Elevated levels of lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] and fibrinogen are known risk factors for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), and their combined elevation in high-risk individuals may amplify risk. However, the long-term impact of this combination on ASCVD incidence in a primary prevention setting remains unclear. This study sought to examine the association between the combination of Lp(a) and fibrinogen with long-term ASCVD risk, in apparently healthy adults from the general population.
METHODS AND RESULTS: A cohort of 3042 CVD-free adults residing in greater Athens, Greece, was recruited in 2002. A 20-year follow-up was conducted in 2022, comprising n = 2169 participants, of which n = 1988 had complete data for cardiovascular disease incidence. Participants were divided into four groups, using a recommended threshold of 30 mg/dL for Lp(a) and the median value of 303 mg/dL for fibrinogen. In the overall cohort, fibrinogen was associated with higher ASCVD risk [hazard ratio (HR) per 10 mg/dL: 1.040, 95%CI:1.009-1.072]. Upon stratification by Lp(a) levels, the significant association was retained and amplified only in individuals with elevated Lp(a) levels (HR 1.083, 95%CI:1.009-1.162) (P for interaction=0.041). Participants with both elevated Lp(a) and fibrinogen levels demonstrated the highest 20-year ASCVD risk (HR 1.904, 95%CI [1.023, 3.547]). Path analysis revealed a mediating role of fibrinogen in the inflammation [i.e. interleukin-6 (IL-6)]-ASCVD risk association, which become more pronounced at higher Lp(a) concentrations.
CONCLUSION: In this general population study, elevated levels of Lp(a) and fibrinogen jointly conferred a higher long-term risk of ASCVD than either marker alone, potentially through the complex involvement of inflammation.

candidates.title: In familial hypercholesterolaemia, remnant cholesterol above 1 mmol/L is associated with 50% higher risk of coronary artery disease.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: Familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH) leads to lifelong elevated low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol and increased risk of coronary artery disease. We tested the hypothesis that elevated remnant cholesterol additionally increases cardiovascular risk in FH.
METHODS: In the Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS) and UK Biobank, 108,751 and 428,625 individuals were classified as with or without FH according to clinical scores and genetic mutations. In the two cohorts, 7,708 and 50,997 experienced coronary artery disease, respectively.
RESULTS: In CGPS and UK Biobank, remnant cholesterol ≥1 mmol/L (39 mg/dL) was observed in 12% and 11% of individuals without FH (N = 104,226 and 403,172), in 33% and 40% with Simon Broome FH (N = 3,923 and 23,860), in 44% and 78% with MEDPED FH (N = 1,005 and 2,465), in 33% and 34% with DLCN FH (N = 744 and 1,207), and in 12% and 21% of individuals with genetic FH (N = 188 and 875). Likewise in the CGPS and UK Biobank, the multivariable adjusted hazard ratios for coronary artery disease by remnant cholesterol ≥1 vs. < 1 mmol/L (39 mg/dL) were 1.49 (95% CI: 1.39-1.59) and 1.47 (1.43-1.52) in individuals without FH, 1.59 (1.31-1.93) and 1.18 (1.10-1.27) in Simon Broome FH, 1.50 (1.08-2.08) and 1.14 (0.89-1.45) in MEDPED FH, 1.60 (1.17-2.21) and 1.59 (1.20-2.09) in DLCN FH, and 1.48 (0.59-3.69) and 1.39 (0.88-2.19) in genetic FH.
CONCLUSION: In familial hypercholesterolaemia, remnant cholesterol ≥1 mmol/L (39 mg/dL) vs below is associated with ≈50% higher risk of coronary artery disease, that is, above the already high risk due to lifelong genetically elevated LDL cholesterol.

candidates.title: Efficacy of fludrocortisone for symptom relief in patients with autonomic syncope and hypotensive phenotype.
candidates.abstract:
AIM: To assess the efficacy of fludrocortisone therapy in patients with autonomic syncope and hypotensive phenotype.
METHODS AND RESULTS: Multicentre, prospective, non-randomized study. Fludrocortisone therapy was guided by clinician experience and supported by two 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) assessments-one before treatment start (ABPM 1) and one after drug optimization (ABPM 2). Primary endpoint: reduction of the syncope burden and presyncopal symptoms based on validated semi structured questionnaires. Secondary endpoint: hypotensive episodes on ABPM. In a cohort of 94 patients treated with fludrocortisone (median age 38 [IQR 21-57]) years, 83% females), 16 patients stopped therapy due to side effects, occurring during optimization (#11) or follow-up (#5). A total of 83 patients were analysed. The average 24-hour systolic blood pressure (SBP) increased from 106.3 ± 8.2 mmHg at ABPM 1 to 112.3 ± 9.3 at ABPM 2 (p = 0.0001). The number of daytime SBP drops <90 mmHg and <100 mmHg decreased by 61%, and 45% respectively (p < 0.001 for both). The annual syncope burden was reduced by 50.2%, from 2.0 (IQR 1.0-4.0) before therapy to 0.0 (IQR 0.0-1.8) episodes during a median follow-up of 12.9 months (p = 0.0001). Subjective symptom improvement was reported by 85.6% of patients. The frequency of syncope/presyncope decreased significantly, p = 0.009. The outcome was similar in 42 younger (23 ± 6 yrs) and in 41 older (56 ± 12 yrs) patients.
CONCLUSION: Fludrocortisone therapy was associated with reduced hypotension and the burden of symptoms both in younger and in older patients. Side effects lead to discontinuation of therapy in 17% of cases.

candidates.title: Impact of CKD and Hemodialysis on Treatment of Severely Calcified Lesions: The ECLIPSE Trial.
candidates.abstract: Background: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) and coronary calcification increase risk for adverse events following drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation. We evaluated whether outcomes following vessel preparation with orbital atherectomy (OA) versus balloon angioplasty (BA) vary according to CKD. Methods: This pre-specified CKD sub-analysis of the prospective, multicenter ECLIPSE trial evaluated 2,001 patients with severely calcified lesions randomized to OA versus BA prior to DES. Independent predictors of two-year target-vessel failure (TVF)-a composite of cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction (TV-MI), or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization (ID-TVR)-were determined using multivariable Cox proportional hazards modeling. Results: CKD (eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m² or hemodialysis) was present in 694 (34.7%) patients; 112 required hemodialysis. Two-year TVF was significantly higher with versus without CKD (21.2% vs. 11.6%; p<0.001), driven by increased cardiac death and ID-TVR. Hemodialysis independently predicted TVF (adjusted HR 2.14, 95% CI 1.30-3.53; p=0.003), whereas reduced eGFR alone did not (p=0.070). In patients on hemodialysis, OA versus BA was associated with higher rates of TVF (52.3% vs. 30.7%; adjusted HR 2.50, 95% CI 1.16-5.41; P=0.020), driven by higher rates of TV-MI and ID-TVR, whereas TVF was similar after OA versus BA in patients not on hemodialysis (13.5% vs. 13.1%; adjusted HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.81-1.35; P=0.730); however, the interaction between treatment assignment and hemodialysis status was not significant (Pint=0.244). Conclusions: CKD remains a major predictor of adverse outcomes after DES implantation in severely calcified lesions, with the highest risks in patients on hemodialysis. In the ECLIPSE trial, higher two-year rates of TVF were observed after vessel preparation with OA compared with BA in patients on hemodialysis but not in patients with CKD not on hemodialysis or in those without CKD. Given the modest hemodialysis subgroup size and non-significant interaction testing, confirmation of these findings in additional studies is warranted.

candidates.title: TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: For patients with moderate aortic stenosis, current guidelines recommend clinical surveillance with echocardiographic assessment every 1 or 2 years. Whether transcatheter aortic-valve replacement (TAVR) will improve outcomes in these patients remains unknown.
METHODS: We conducted an international, open-label, randomized trial to evaluate whether TAVR will result in better outcomes than clinical surveillance among patients with moderate aortic stenosis with at least one at-risk feature (i.e., a symptom or structural or functional abnormality that has been shown to be associated with faster disease progression or adverse cardiovascular outcomes). The patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo transfemoral TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance. The primary effectiveness end point was a composite of death from any cause or a heart-failure event with or without hospitalization at 2 years. Superiority testing was performed in the intention-to-treat population.
RESULTS: A total of 744 patients underwent randomization: 373 patients were assigned to the TAVR group and 371 to the clinical-surveillance group. The mean age of patients was 78 years, 39.1% were women, and 45.6% were at low surgical risk. The mean aortic-valve area was 1.2 cm2, and the mean aortic-valve peak velocity was 3.3 m per second. At 2 years, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients with a primary effectiveness end-point event was 16.7% in the TAVR group and 23.9% in the clinical-surveillance group (risk difference, -7.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -13.1 to -1.3; P = 0.02 for superiority). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients who died from any cause was 8.4% in the TAVR group and 7.3% in the clinical-surveillance group; the estimates for a heart-failure event were 10.8% and 19.0%, respectively. The incidence of procedure-related adverse events did not differ meaningfully between the patients in the TAVR group and those in the clinical-surveillance group who underwent aortic-valve replacement.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with moderate aortic stenosis and at-risk features, a strategy of TAVR was superior to clinical surveillance in lowering the incidence of death or a heart-failure event at 2 years. (Funded by Edwards Lifesciences; PROGRESS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04889872.).

candidates.title: Antithrombotic Therapy After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: The SIMPLAAFY Randomized Clinical Trial.
candidates.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Following a left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) procedure, antithrombotic therapy is administered to safely allow time for device endothelialization. However, the optimal postimplant antithrombotic regimen is unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To determine if either reduced-dose non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants (NOACs) or aspirin alone are noninferior to dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for the composite clinical end point of death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding through 6 months post LAAC.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This open-label, 3-group, multicenter clinical trial randomized 1857 patients between October 2024 and December 2025 at 87 US investigational sites, with the final 6-month follow-up in July 2026. Enrolled patients had nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, underwent successful LAAC, and were eligible for all 3 regimens.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly allocated 1:1:1 to DAPT for 6 months followed by aspirin (n = 624), a reduced-dose NOAC for 3 months followed by aspirin (n = 620), or aspirin alone for 12 months (n = 613).
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the 6-month composite of all-cause death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding. Noninferiority was tested in the primary analysis population with a 1-sided Farrington-Manning test (α = .025). Bleeding and 45-day device-related thrombus rates were exploratory without multiplicity adjustment.
RESULTS: The cohort had a mean age of 76 (SD, 8) years, 42.9% were female, the mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4.2 (SD, 1.3), and 68.0% had paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. The primary outcome occurred in 41 patients (6.9%) with DAPT vs 31 (5.1%) with a reduced-dose NOAC (risk ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.48-1.18]; risk difference, -1.7 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, 1.2) and 20 (3.3%) with aspirin alone (risk ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.29-0.82]; risk difference, -3.5 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, -0.8). Both monotherapy strategies met noninferiority criteria (P < .001 for noninferiority for both). Major bleeding was 4.5% with DAPT, 2.7% with reduced-dose NOACs, and 1.7% with aspirin alone; clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was 8.7%, 4.8%, and 3.8%, respectively. Device-related thrombus was observed in 3.4%, 0.9%, and 2.7%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Both reduced-dose NOACs and aspirin alone were noninferior to DAPT for 6-month outcomes after uncomplicated LAAC.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06521463.

candidates.title: Rotational Atherectomy Plus Intravascular Lithotripsy Versus Intravascular Lithotripsy Alone for Coronary Calcified Nodules: The NODULE-SHOCK Trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal lesion preparation for coronary calcified nodules (CNs) and intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) pulse delivery for severe calcification remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate phenotype-specific calcium modification in severe calcification with and without CNs.
METHODS: In this single-center randomized trial using a new-generation coronary IVL catheter, patients with optical coherence tomography-defined CNs (Cohort A) were assigned 1:1 to rotational atherectomy (RA) plus IVL or IVL alone; patients with severe calcification without CNs (Cohort B) were assigned 1:1 to maximum or operator-determined IVL pulses. Primary endpoints were minimum stent area (MSA) at the CN site in Cohort A and at the maximum calcium arc site in Cohort B.
RESULTS: Among 120 patients, 66 (55%) were in Cohort A (33 per group) and 54 (45%) in Cohort B (27 per group). MSA at the CN site was 7.41 ± 2.12 mm2 with RA plus IVL vs 6.23 ± 1.55 mm2 with IVL alone (mean difference: 1.18 mm2; 95% CI: 0.27-2.09; P = 0.012). In Cohort B, MSA at the maximum calcium arc site was 5.50 ± 1.19 mm2 with maximum IVL pulses vs 5.56 ± 1.45 mm2 with operator-determined IVL pulses (mean difference: -0.06 mm2; 95% CI: -0.78 to 0.67; P = 0.873).
CONCLUSIONS: RA plus IVL increased final stent area vs IVL alone in CN lesions, whereas maximum IVL pulses did not significantly increase final stent area compared with operator-determined pulses in severe calcification without CNs. These findings warrant validation in larger multicenter trials with clinical endpoints. (Coronary Calcified Nodule Management With Rotational Atherectomy Plus Shockwave Intravascular Lithotripsy vs Intravascular Lithotripsy Alone: A Prospective, Randomized Trial [NODULE-SHOCK]; ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07000045).

candidates.title: 1-Year Safety and Effectiveness of a Next-Generation Dual-Seal Left Atrial Appendage Occluder.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is a stroke prevention alternative for patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) intolerant to long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC). The next-generation dual-seal device was designed to improve operator ease of use while maintaining effective LAAO of the predicate device.
OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this analysis was to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of a next-generation device through 1 year.
METHODS: VERITAS is a single-arm, prospective, global, multicenter study. Patients with nonvalvular AF with an increased thromboembolism risk seeking a nonpharmacologic alternative to OAC were enrolled. One-year descriptive endpoints are provided, including mortality, neurological events, major bleeding, and device-related complications. One-year cardiac imaging was assessed for peridevice leak and device-related thrombus (DRT).
RESULTS: Complete left atrial appendage (LAA) closure (0 mm leak) was observed in 91.1% (95% CI: 87.9%-93.7%) of patients by either transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) or cardiac computed tomography and 96.3% (95% CI: 93.2%-98.2%) by TEE alone. The cumulative DRT rate was 3.3% (95% CI: 2.0%-5.3%) with only 0.4% (95% CI: 0.1%-1.5%) deemed clinically relevant. One-year key clinical outcome rates are as follows: all-cause mortality: 3.9% (95% CI: 2.4%-6.3%); cardiovascular mortality: 1.9% (95% CI: 0.9%-3.8%); major bleeding: 6.6% (95% CI: 4.5%-9.2%); ischemic stroke or systemic embolism: 1.8% (95% CI: 0.8%-3.3%); pericardial effusion requiring intervention: 0.9% (95% CI: 0.3%-2.1%). No (0%) device embolization occurred. Median follow-up was 365 days (IQR: 349-380 days).
CONCLUSIONS: The VERITAS study results support the 1-year safety and effectiveness of the next-generation device. (Abbott Medical-VERITAS Study; NCT06707688).

candidates.title: TECTONIC CAD: Pivotal IDE Evaluation of Coronary Intravascular Lithotripsy for Severely Calcified Lesions.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe coronary calcification complicates percutaneous coronary intervention by limiting lesion compliance and impairing stent expansion.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the SonicForce Coronary Intravascular Lithotripsy System (Abbott Vascular) in severely calcified de novo coronary lesions.
METHODS: TECTONIC CAD intravascular lithotripsy investigational device exemption (NCT06885177) was a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study of 335 patients at 40 U.S.
CENTERS: The primary safety endpoint was 30-day target lesion failure, defined as cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target lesion revascularization. The primary effectiveness endpoint was procedural success. Each endpoint was tested against a prespecified performance goal. A prespecified optical coherence tomography (OCT) substudy evaluated calcium modification and stent expansion.
RESULTS: A total of 335 patients were included in the full analysis set, with 330 and 334 as the evaluable populations for the primary safety and primary effectiveness endpoints, respectively, and a median follow-up duration of 36 days (Q1-Q3: 28-37 days). Thirty-day target lesion failure was 0.3% (1 of 330; exact 2-sided 95% CI: 0.0%-1.7%); the upper 1-sided 97.5% confidence bound was 1.7%, below the 12.9% performance goal (P < 0.0001). Procedural success was 97.0% (324 of 334; exact 2-sided 95% CI: 94.6%-98.6%); the lower 1-sided 97.5% confidence bound was 94.6%, above the 87.1% performance goal (P < 0.0001). In the OCT substudy, mean calcium length was 22.2 ± 10.3 mm, and the maximum contiguous calcium site had a calcium arc of 247.3 ± 99.0° and a thickness of 0.90 ± 0.25 mm at baseline. At this site, final stent area was 7.1 ± 1.9 mm2, with stent expansion of 95.9% ± 18.6%. Calcium fracture was identified in 62.5% (50 of 80) of lesions after intravascular lithotripsy and 66.3% (53 of 80) after stenting.
CONCLUSIONS: TECTONIC CAD met both prespecified coprimary safety and effectiveness endpoints, demonstrating low 30-day target lesion failure and high procedural success. OCT demonstrated calcium fracture and favorable stent expansion at maximum contiguous calcium.

candidates.title: Coronary CT Angiography versus Intravascular Ultrasound Guidance for PCI.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves clinical outcomes. Coronary computed tomographic angiography (CCTA) provides anatomical and physiological information before cardiac catheterization that may enable PCI planning. Data regarding the use of CCTA-guided PCI as compared with IVUS-guided PCI with respect to clinical outcomes are lacking.
METHODS: In this investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized, noninferiority trial with blinded end-point adjudication, we randomly assigned patients with a clinical indication for revascularization, at least one epicardial lesion with a diameter stenosis of more than 70%, and a fractional flow reserve derived from CCTA of 0.80 or less in a 1:1 ratio to a CCTA-guided or IVUS-guided PCI strategy. The primary end point was target-vessel failure, defined as a composite of death from cardiac causes, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization, at 12 months. The noninferiority margin for the absolute risk difference was 4.5 percentage points, with a prespecified hierarchical testing strategy for superiority.
RESULTS: A total of 1105 patients underwent randomization: 556 to the CCTA-guided PCI group and 549 to the IVUS-guided PCI group. The median age of the patients was 65 years, and 21.7% were women. At 12 months, target-vessel failure had occurred in 23 patients (4.1%) in the CCTA-guided PCI group and in 25 patients (4.6%) in the IVUS-guided PCI group (risk difference, -0.42 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -2.82 to 1.99; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.73 for superiority). A total of 6 patients in the CCTA-guided PCI group and 9 patients in the IVUS-guided PCI group had clinical procedural complications.
CONCLUSIONS: A CCTA-guided PCI strategy was noninferior to IVUS-guided PCI with respect to target-vessel failure at 12 months. (Funded by GE HealthCare and Heartflow; P4 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05253677.).

candidates.title: Antecedent Kidney Function and Cardiovascular Mortality in Over 300 000 Patients With Incident Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease is a frequent comorbidity in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and has been proposed as a contributor to its development. However, the spectrum of antecedent kidney function before incident HFpEF and its association with subsequent cardiovascular outcomes remains unclear.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter cohort study across 170 US Veterans Affairs hospitals, including patients with incident HFpEF diagnosed between January 1, 2000, and June 30, 2025. HFpEF was ascertained using natural language processing-derived left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50% closest to the incident HF date and a validated HFpEF algorithm incorporating loop diuretic use, elevated natriuretic peptide levels, and an HFpEF-age, body mass index, and atrial fibrillation score >0.5. Antecedent kidney function was classified using 2 estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) measurements obtained ≥90 days apart before incident HFpEF and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio. We characterized antecedent kidney function, including albuminuria (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/g), and examined its associations with 5-year cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization. Competing-risk analysis was performed accounting for noncardiovascular death as a competing event for cardiovascular death.
RESULTS: Of 304 712 patients meeting HFpEF ascertainment criteria, 236 910 comprised the final cohort; 51% had antecedent eGFR ≥60 mL/min per 1.73m2. Overall, 15% had an eGFR ≥90 mL/min per 1.73m2. Patients with eGFR <60 mL/min per 1.73m2 were older and had more diabetes and hypertension. 51% of the patients with eGFR <60 mL/min per 1.73m2 had body mass index <30 kg/m2, including 20% with body mass index <25 kg/m2. Progressively lower antecedent kidney function was associated with graded increases in cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization. Among decedents, the proportion of deaths attributed to cardiovascular causes increased from 25% in the preserved eGFR (≥90 mL/min per 1.73m2) without documented albuminuria to 32% with albuminuria and 38% with advanced kidney dysfunction (P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide study of patients with incident HFpEF, antecedent kidney dysfunction was common but not uniformly present before HFpEF onset. Furthermore, among patients who developed HFpEF, antecedent kidney dysfunction identified a higher-risk phenotype, with progressively greater cardiovascular mortality and heart failure hospitalization with declining kidney function.

candidates.title: Performance of the PREVENT-HF Equations Across Heart Failure Subtypes in Community-Based and Ambulatory Healthcare Samples.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The PREVENT-HF equations estimate 10-year risk of overall heart failure (HF), inclusive of both HF with preserved and reduced ejection fraction (HFpEF; HFrEF). Given differential risk factor profiles, pathophysiology, and therapeutic strategies for each HF subtype, we sought to examine the performance of PREVENT-HF for subtype-specific risk assessment.
METHODS: We included data from five pooled longitudinal cohort studies (baseline exam 1989 to 2013) and two longitudinal primary-care electronic health record-based samples (Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center [BIDMC], baseline 2004 to 2014; Mass General Brigham [MGB], baseline 2001 to 2018). We assessed the performance of the PREVENT-HF equations in predicting 10-year incident HFrEF and HFpEF, including model discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC]; average precision [AP]/event rate) and calibration (integrated calibration index [ICI]), in adults aged 30-79 years without prevalent cardiovascular disease or HF.
RESULTS: The pooled cohort studies included 23,652 (55% women, age 60 ± 13 years), of whom 1,232 developed HF (432 [35%] HFpEF, 522 [42%] HFrEF). The BIDMC sample included 29,815 (55% women, 50 ± 13 years), of whom 259 (1%) developed HF (133 [51%] HFpEF, 101 [39%] HFrEF). MGB included 138,999 (62% women, 52 ± 13 years), of whom 1050 developed HF (586 [56%] HFpEF, 381 [36%] HFrEF). PREVENT-HF demonstrated better discrimination for HFpEF than HFrEF across all samples: in the pooled cohorts, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.824 (95% CI 0.807, 0.839) versus 0.789 (95% CI 0.770, 0.807) for HFrEF; in BIDMC, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.897 (95% CI 0.874, 0.918) versus 0.833 (95% CI 0.791, 0.869) for HFrEF; in MGB, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.864 (95% CI 0.848, 0.880) versus 0.797 (95% CI 0.771, 0.820) for HFrEF. Similar results were reflected in the AP/event rate ratios: 2.92 (95% CI 2.47, 3.54) for HFpEF compared to 2.66 (95% CI 2.33, 3.14) for HFrEF in the pooled cohorts; 8.08 (95% CI 6.12, 12.30) for HFpEF compared to 5.12 (95% CI 3.84, 8.17) for HFrEF in BIDMC; and 6.84 (95% CI 5.66, 8.28) for HFpEF compared to 4.12 (95% CI 3.37, 5.16) for HFrEF in MGB. Calibration was similar for HFpEF and HFrEF across samples. For example, in the pooled cohorts, the ICI for HFpEF was 0.041 (95% CI 0.039, 0.043) and for HFrEF was 0.038 (95% CI 0.036, 0.040).
CONCLUSIONS: PREVENT-HF demonstrated excellent discrimination for both HF subtypes across community-based cohorts and real-world samples, with consistently better discrimination for HFpEF as compared to HFrEF. Given PREVENT-HF was developed to estimate overall HF risk rather than subtype-specific risk, future studies are needed to establish subtype-specific risk thresholds.

candidates.title: Prevalence of Angiographic Coronary Artery Disease in Systolic Heart Failure Without Infarct-Pattern Late Gadolinium Enhancement: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: Rest late gadolinium enhancement cardiovascular magnetic resonance (LGE-CMR) identifies infarct-pattern scar but does not assess coronary anatomy. We estimated the prevalence of angiographic coronary artery disease (CAD) among adults with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) or otherwise unexplained left ventricular systolic dysfunction without infarct-pattern LGE.
METHODS AND RESULTS: MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched to 27 July 2026. Eligible studies provided separable scar-negative denominators and corresponding angiographic CAD counts from invasive coronary angiography (ICA). Scar-negative was defined as the absence of subendocardial or transmural LGE in a coronary distribution. Random-effects logit meta-analysis used restricted maximum likelihood and Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals. Twenty-two reports representing 20 studies included 2,236 paired LGE-CMR and ICA. 818 patients had infarct-pattern scar, and 1,418 were scar-negative. Eight studies contributed 44 CAD cases among 468 scar-negative patients for ≥50% stenosis, giving a pooled prevalence of 10.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] 7.4-15.4). Five studies contributed 19 CAD cases among 271 scar-negative patients for ≥70% stenosis, giving a pooled prevalence of 7.6% (95% CI 4.4-12.6). Seven studies contributed 33 CAD cases among 679 scar-negative patients for high-risk-pattern CAD, giving a pooled prevalence of 4.9% (95% CI 2.2-10.6) and a 95% prediction interval of 0.8-24.8%. These strata represented different study subsets and were not nested.
CONCLUSION: Among selected adults with HFrEF or otherwise unexplained LVSD who underwent paired LGE-CMR and ICA, absence of infarct-pattern LGE did not exclude angiographic CAD. Further coronary assessment should be considered when resolving that uncertainty would alter diagnosis or management.

candidates.title: Controversy: Anticoagulants need to be maintained after catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation in patients at risk of stroke-Pro and Contra.
candidates.abstract: The pillars of atrial fibrillation (AF) management include stroke prevention, patient-centred symptom directed decisions on rhythm or rate control, and the proactive management of comorbidities and lifestyle changes. These pillars are not in isolation; they are complementary to each other. While oral anticoagulants (OACs) are highly effective for reducing stroke and all-cause mortality in patients with AF, these drugs confer a risk of major bleeding, including intracranial bleeding. Evidence from clinical trials and observational data shows that early rhythm control, especially with catheter ablation, results in a reduction in stroke risk and/or the reduction in AF burden. The question arises therefore, whether in patients with intermediate or low stroke risk after successful catheter ablation, whether or not to continue or discontinue OAC. Recent randomized trials and observational data have created some debate about whether OAC can be routinely stopped after a successful catheter ablation procedure, without a higher risk of thromboembolism. In this pro/contra article, we will debate the arguments for and against the cessation of anti-coagulation after catheter ablation, in the context of recent evidence from clinical trials, observational data, and meta-analysis.

candidates.title: Remote activity and rhythm monitoring using patient-owned consumer devices after first-time pulmonary vein isolation.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Passively collected physical activity data from consumer devices could provide a scalable, objective measure of functional status in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). This study assessed the feasibility of remotely collecting activity and rhythm data from patients undergoing index pulmonary vein isolation (PVI).
METHODS: AF patients enrolled in the prospective TRUST registry who underwent index PVI and reported owning an eligible smartphone were re-contacted to provide informed consent and share their smartphone- and smartwatch-generated data. Pre-specified feasibility criteria were participation rate, technical success, and temporal data coverage. The primary functional outcome was the mean daily step-count change between the one-year pre-PVI and two-year post-PVI windows. Exploratory analyses examined associations of daily activity with AF recurrence and AF burden.
RESULTS: Of 280 eligible patients, 172 (61%) attempted and 154/172 (90%) completed data transfer, of whom 123 met pre-specified completeness criteria. Median monitoring duration was 6.0 [3.6, 6.6] years, with 98% [77, 100] coverage. Mean daily step count increased from 5731±2808 to 6220±2816 steps/day after PVI (+488 steps/day [187, 789]; p=0.002). In 35 smartwatch users, AF burden decreased from 3.6% [1.6, 10.8] to 0.0% [0.0, 0.3] after PVI (p<0.001). Baseline AF burden was inversely correlated with daily step count (ρ=-0.36, p=0.035).
CONCLUSION: Remote collection of activity and rhythm data from consumer smartphones and smartwatches is feasible, yielding high-coverage, multi-year research data. This enables scalable, objective quantification of longitudinal functional outcomes. Daily step count increased after PVI in this exploratory cohort and was inversely related to baseline AF burden.

candidates.title: PCSK9-Targeting Therapies and Mortality: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the association of PCSK9-targeting therapies with mortality and cardiovascular events in stable or clinically stabilized randomized trial populations.
METHODS: We systematically reviewed randomized trials comparing alirocumab, evolocumab or inclisiran with placebo or active control. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261395609). Treatment effects were pooled as incidence rate ratios (IRRs) using random-effects models. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Prespecified subgroup analyses were based on trial-level known atherosclerosis status, as defined by enrollment criteria.
RESULTS: Thirty-two trials enrolled 77,178 participants. Individual atherosclerosis status could not be determined beyond trial-level eligibility criteria. Mortality estimates were predominantly informed by large cardiovascular outcome trials. All-cause mortality was lower with PCSK9-targeting therapy (IRR 0.88, 95% CI 0.82-0.95). Estimates favored PCSK9-targeting treatment in both trials requiring known atherosclerosis for enrollment (IRR 0.90, 95% CI 0.83-0.98) and trials without such an enrollment requirement (IRR 0.78, 95% CI 0.62-0.97; interaction p = 0.21). PCSK9-targeting treatment additionally reduced myocardial infarction, stroke, and coronary revascularization rates. Leave-one-out estimates remained directionally consistent.
CONCLUSION: PCSK9-targeting therapies were associated with lower all-cause mortality and fewer ischemic events across trial populations. The predominant contribution of large cardiovascular outcome trials enrolling populations with known atherosclerosis and using PCSK9 antibodies limits the ability to infer a survival benefit in populations not selected on the basis of atherosclerosis status and across individual therapies, particularly inclisiran.

candidates.title: Microvascular Resistance Reserve and Outcomes in Angina and Nonobstructive Coronary Artery Disease.
candidates.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is highly prevalent in patients with angina and nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA). Microvascular resistance reserve (MRR) is a novel index to assess CMD independently of epicardial disease and driving pressures, but the long-term prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR in patients with ANOCA is unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR and its association with clinical outcomes and symptom burden in patients with ANOCA.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This prospective, multicenter cohort study within the Netherlands Registry of Invasive Coronary Vasomotor Function Testing (NL-CFT) included patients between July 2020 and June 2025 in 4 clinical centers in the Netherlands. Follow-up for clinical events and patient-reported symptoms was completed for up to 3 years. Clinical events were adjudicated by investigators blinded to CFT results. Consecutive patients with ANOCA who underwent continuous thermodilution were included.
EXPOSURE: Abnormal MRR (CMD) was defined as less than 2.1, gray zone as 2.1 to 2.7, and normal microvascular function as 2.7 or greater.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary clinical outcome was a composite of all-cause death, acute coronary syndrome, stroke, clinically indicated revascularization, repeat angiography without intervention, and unplanned hospital admittance or emergency department visit due to angina or heart failure. Secondary outcomes included angina at baseline and follow-up. Symptoms were assessed using the patient-reported Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ) scores.
RESULTS: Among 553 included patients (mean [SD] age, 59.1 [9.6] years; 459 female [83.0%]) with a mean (SD) follow-up of 27.5 (16.1) months, CMD was observed in 94 patients (17.0%). The main composite outcome did not differ across the 3 MRR categories (18 of 94 patients with abnormal [19.1%] vs 21 of 98 patients with gray zone [21.4%] vs 76 of 361 patients with normal [21.1%] MRR; log-rank P = .85). Individual outcomes did not differ between groups. There was no overall longitudinal interaction between MRR and SAQ summary scores. While low MRR (abnormal vs normal groups) was not associated with an increased symptom burden at baseline, it was associated with worse angina at follow-up (mean [SD] SAQ summary score, 53.0 [16.7] vs 60.1 [16.6]; P = .04) and less clinically relevant improvement (9 of 30 patients [30.0%] vs 52 of 88 patients [59.1%]; P = .02).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, CMD assessed by continuous thermodilution-derived MRR was not associated with clinical outcomes.

candidates.title: Behavior-Based Electrogram Mapping Identifies Potential Functional Substrates in Atrial Fibrillation: The KSP-AF Randomized Study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Conventional substrate mapping during atrial fibrillation (AF) may fail to capture dynamic electrogram behavior. Key spatiotemporal potentials (KSPs) are electrogram patterns identified by their temporal behavior during AF. We evaluated whether KSP-guided ablation improves outcomes beyond pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) and characterized their short-term frequency consistency.
METHODS: In this single-center randomized study, 100 patients with paroxysmal or persistent AF undergoing first-time ablation were assigned to PVI plus KSP-guided ablation or PVI alone. The primary endpoint was 24-month single-procedure freedom from documented AF recurrence without antiarrhythmic drugs. Dominant frequency (DF) analysis included 93 KSP regions from 18 patients, assessed across four consecutive 5-second epochs.
RESULTS: Acute AF termination occurred in 68% of patients with PVI + KSP versus 26% with PVI alone (P < 0.001). At 24 months, freedom from AF recurrence was 74% versus 48% (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.18-0.79; P = 0.010), and freedom from AF/atrial tachycardia recurrence was 68% versus 46% (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.25-0.97; P = 0.040). Within-recording temporal DF variability was low (coefficient of variation, 4.8 ± 1.2%).
CONCLUSION: Adding KSP-guided ablation to PVI improved acute and 24-month rhythm outcomes in this single-center trial. These findings support further evaluation of behavior-based mapping to identify potential functional AF substrates and require multicenter confirmation.

candidates.title: Posterior Leaflet Restoration for Secondary Mitral Regurgitation: EXPLORE MR Results.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Secondary mitral regurgitation (MR) contributes to morbidity and mortality in patients with symptomatic valve disease. Although transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is beneficial, many patients remain suboptimal candidates. Posterior leaflet restoration (PLR) provides a prosthetic coaptation surface via an adaptive coaptation element that inflates during systole and deflates during diastole to facilitate leaflet coaptation.
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the safety and feasibility of PLR using the MRace implant (Polares Medical, Inc).
METHODS: Early Feasibility Experience of Posterior Leaflet Restoration to Reduce Mitral Regurgitation Using the MRace Implant in Georgia and Brazil (EXPLORE MR) enrolled 78 symptomatic patients with severe secondary MR (≥3+), stratified post hoc by left ventricular end-diastolic volume: nonseverely enlarged left ventricle (NSELV) (N = 46) and severely enlarged left ventricle (SELV) (N = 32). The primary endpoint was 30-day mortality; secondary endpoints were MR reduction and functional outcomes.
RESULTS: The implant was successfully deployed in 96.2% of patients. All-cause mortality at 30 days was 6.4%. MR ≤2+ was achieved in 93.8% of patients at 30 days and was sustained in 90.6% at 1 year. Patients with NSELV showed better results in MR ≤1+ at every time point (94.4% at 30 days, 89.5% at 1 year) compared with the SELV group (79.3% and 69.2%, respectively). The NSELV subgroup demonstrated better functional recovery, with NYHA functional class I or II rising from 8.7% to 84.2%, vs a more attenuated response in the SELV group (15.6%-76.9%). The 6-minute walk test improved in the paired NSELV cohort (Δ +93.9 m), but not in paired patients with SELV (Δ -7.8 m). Kaplan-Meier 1-year all-cause mortality was 29.5% overall and was better in patients with NSELV (19.4%) than in SELV (41.7%).
CONCLUSIONS: PLR with the MRace implant achieves substantial MR reduction and meaningful functional improvement, most pronounced in patients without severely enlarged left ventricles. (XPLORE MRace [BR]: Early Feasibility Experience of Posterior Leaflet Restoration to Reduce Mitral Regurgitation Using the MRace Implant [EXPLORE MRace]; NCT06113354).

candidates.title: Utility of Donor-Recipient HLA Matching in Heart Transplantation in the Era of Extended Donor Organ Preservation: A Multi-Institutional Analysis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Closer human leukocyte antigen (HLA) match between the donor and the recipient leads to better outcomes after kidney transplantation. Since extended donor preservation is now possible in heart transplantation (HT), we examined the possible impact of prioritization of HLA matching in HT.
METHODS: We included single organ HT recipients reported to the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN) transplanted in 2010-2019. Outcomes included survival, treated rejection and development of cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV) across 5 and 10 year follow-up after transplant. We examined associations between matches at A, B, DR, DPB, DQA, DQB and DPA loci and the outcomes in univariable and multivariable analyses.
RESULTS: There were 5176 patients in the 5Y cohort with a median of 9 (IQR 8; 11) HLA mismatches and 9118 patients in the 10Y cohort with a median of 6 (IQR 5; 7) HLA mismatches. In adjusted analyses, there was no significant association between donor-recipient HLA match and mortality, treated rejection or CAV in the 5Y cohort. In the 10Y cohort, HLA mismatch was a risk factor for mortality (HR 1.06, CI 1; 1.12, p=0.047) and treated rejection (HR 1.13, CI 1.07;1.2, p<0.001) in adults. Among pediatric patients, HLA mismatch conferred a nominally higher risk of mortality (HR 1.14, CI 0.97; 1.34, p=0.121) and treated rejection (HR 1.08, CI 0.96;1.21, p=0.226).
CONCLUSIONS: We show that the current impact of donor-recipient HLA match on post-HT outcomes is relatively small. While novel organ preservation techniques may make HLA matching feasible, our data do not support its adoption into future iterations of the HT allocation system.

candidates.title: Hemodynamic Effects of Reducing LV Afterload With Impella or Intra-Aortic Balloon Counterpulsation During Veno-Arterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Cardiogenic Shock: HERACLES Trial.
candidates.abstract: Background: Veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) provides organ support in cardiogenic shock but increases left ventricular (LV) afterload, potentially impairing cardiac recovery. LV unloading with an intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) or micro-axial flow pump (mAFP) may mitigate this effect. HERACLES compared their effects on myocardial oxygen supply and demand. Methods: Patients receiving VA-ECMO for cardiogenic shock were randomized to LV unloading with IABP or mAFP, stratified by ischemic/non-ischemic etiology. Distal coronary, aortic and LV pressures and coronary flow (inverse mean transit time, Tmn) were measured with and without unloading. Myocardial oxygen demand was estimated as the area under the LV pressure curve in systole (TTI) x heart rate (HR). The primary endpoint was the change in myocardial oxygen supply-demand ratio calculated as [(Tmn * TTI*HR)off / (Tmn * TTI *HR)unload]. Secondary endpoints included changes in coronary flow [device flow ratio (DFR) =(Tmn)off/ (Tmn)unload], oxygen demand per beat (DTTI), contractility (DdP/dtmax) and filling pressure (DLVEDP). Results: Twenty-four patients were enrolled (age 51 [46-57]; 46% male; 96% SCAI D/E; 38% ischemic). At randomization, lactate was 4.3 mmol/L [IQR 2.5 to 8.4], LV ejection fraction 10% [10 to 17], LVEDP 18 mmHg [14 to 24]. The myocardial oxygen supply-demand ratio improved with IABP but not mAFP (1.48 [1.23 to 2.10] vs 0.97 [0.92 to 1.39]; P=0.036), driven predominantly by differential reduction of TTI. Coronary pressure increased but flow was unchanged with mAFP (DFR 1.00 [0.86 to 1.13]). Coronary flow increased marginally with IABP (DFR 1.16 [1.00 to 1.51]). LV pressures decreased with both devices and contractility with IABP only, with no between-group differences. Thirty-day mortality was similar (38% vs 45%, p=0.84). Conclusions: In VA-ECMO supported SCAI D/E cardiogenic shock, IABP improved myocardial oxygen supply-demand balance, whereas mAFP did not. Further research is needed to determine whether these mechanistic differences translate to clinical outcomes.

candidates.title: Bivalirudin With a High-Dose Post-PCI Infusion Versus Heparin During Primary PCI in STEMI: One-Year Results From the BRIGHT-4 Trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The BRIGHT-4 trial (Bivalirudin With Prolonged Full-Dose Infusion During Primary PCI Versus Heparin Trial-4) demonstrated that procedural anticoagulation with bivalirudin plus a high-dose postprocedure infusion reduced the 30-day composite end point of all-cause death or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 3 to 5 bleeding compared with heparin monotherapy in patients with ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with radial artery access. We now report the 12-month follow-up results to evaluate the long-term outcomes of primary PCI with these 2 anticoagulation regimens.
METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized controlled trial, 6016 patients with ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary PCI with radial artery access were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive bivalirudin with a high-dose post-PCI infusion for 2 to 4 hours (n=3009) or heparin monotherapy (n=3007). The primary outcome of interest was the composite of all-cause death or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 3 to 5 bleeding at 12 months.
RESULTS: At 12 months, the primary outcome occurred in 124 (4.1%) patients in the bivalirudin group and 169 (5.6%) patients in the heparin group (hazard ratio, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.58-0.92]; P=0.007). Bivalirudin resulted in lower 12-month rates of Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 3 to 5 bleeding (0.6% versus 1.2%; hazard ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.28-0.87]; P=0.01) and stent thrombosis (0.8% versus 1.3%; hazard ratio, 0.60 [95% CI, 0.36-0.99]; P=0.045), with nonsignificant differences in all-cause death (3.8% versus 4.8%; hazard ratio, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.63-1.02]; P=0.08), cardiovascular death, reinfarction, ischemia-driven target vessel revascularization, and stroke between the 2 groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary PCI with radial artery access, the benefits of bivalirudin with a high-dose post-PCI infusion in reducing the composite end point of all-cause death or Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types 3 to 5 bleeding at 30 days compared with heparin monotherapy are maintained through 12-month follow-up. These findings support the use of bivalirudin with a post-PCI high-dose infusion as an alternative to heparin to reduce mortality and major bleeding in patients with ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction.

candidates.title: Omega-3 Fatty Acids and Atrial Fibrillation: Current Evidence and Expert Opinion.
candidates.abstract: Recent clinical trials have reported an increased risk for atrial fibrillation (AF) in individuals treated with omega-3 fatty acids (FA). As virtually all these studies were conducted with pharmaceutical omega-3 FA preparations in populations at higher risk for cardiovascular disease (CVD), it is unclear to what extent these findings apply to the general population consuming omega-3 FA either from oily fish or from omega-3 FA supplements. Based on an updated meta-analysis reviewed here, consumption of up to 1500 mg/day (and possibly 2400 mg/day) of eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) + docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) from food or dietary supplements in the general adult population does not appear to significantly increase risk for AF. Indeed, the preponderance of the evidence suggests that chronic intakes in this range are associated with lower risk for AF (and other CVD outcomes) in the general population. For individuals at high risk for CVD, treatment with EPA+DHA doses of >1500 mg/day might increase the absolute risk for AF (by <1%) and the relative risk (by ∼43%). Because of the favorable effects of EPA+DHA on CVD (and other health) outcomes, our view is that, for the general population, intakes of EPA+DHA afford several health benefits and do not meaningfully increase the risk for AF. For patients with prevalent CVD or at high risk for CVD, the risk-benefit ratio for EPA+DHA intake is favorable, especially for intakes up to 1500 mg/day, but also at higher doses where there may be increased risk for AF.

candidates.title: Prognostic Impact of Discharge Transprosthetic Tricuspid Gradient After Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement: The TRIPLACE Registry.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although transprosthetic gradients are established prognostic markers after left-sided valve interventions, the prognostic significance of discharge tricuspid gradient (dTVG) after transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) remains unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the association between dTVG and clinical outcomes after TTVR and identify high dTVG determinants.
METHODS: TRIPLACE (Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement) is an international, multicenter TTVR registry. A discharge landmark analysis was performed, excluding patients with in-hospital mortality, lack of TTVR technical success, missing dTVG, or unavailable follow-up at any time point. Endpoints included all-cause mortality and the composite of all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization. The optimal dTVG cutoff was identified through quartile-based survival analysis and confirmed by log-rank maximization. Multivariable Cox models were developed using cross-validated candidate variable selection.
RESULTS: Among 526 patients, 474 were included. Median follow-up was 208.5 days (Q1-Q3: 54-474 days). A data-driven dTVG cutoff of 3.5 mm Hg identified 122 of 474 patients (25.7%) with high dTVG. dTVG ≥3.5 mm Hg was associated with higher 1- and 3-year mortality (HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.14-3.75; P = 0.017 and HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.24-3.48; P = 0.006, respectively) and composite endpoint events (HR: 1.99; 95% CI: 1.31-3.03; P = 0.001 and HR: 1.96; 95% CI: 1.33-2.88; P < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, dTVG ≥3.5 mm Hg remained associated with 3-year mortality (adjusted HR: 1.84; 95% CI: 1.09-3.10; P = 0.022) and the composite endpoint at 1 and 3 years (adjusted HR: 1.77; 95% CI: 1.16-2.70; P = 0.009 and adjusted HR: 1.77; 95% CI: 1.20-2.60; P = 0.004, respectively). Indexed inner transcatheter tricuspid valve diameter was the only potentially modifiable independent predictor of high dTVG (OR: 0.79 per 1 mm/m2 increase; 95% CI: 0.71-0.88).
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated dTVG after TTVR independently identifies patients at increased risk of adverse outcomes. A 3.5 mm Hg threshold may support postprocedural risk stratification, whereas inner valve diameter represents a potentially modifiable determinant of elevated dTVG. (TRIPLACE [Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement]; NCT06033274).

candidates.title: Evaluation of an Echocardiography-Based Artificial Intelligence Algorithm for Early HFpEF Detection: A HeartShare/AMP-HF Cohort Study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is difficult to identify because of nonspecific symptoms and subtle echocardiographic abnormalities. EchoGo HF, an FDA-cleared artificial intelligence (AI) model, estimates HFpEF probability from a single apical 4-chamber echocardiographic clip, but has been validated only in patients with clinically adjudicated HFpEF.
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate whether AI-HFpEF can detect early HFpEF in community-dwelling adults without a clinical heart failure (HF) diagnosis and predict incident clinical HFpEF in patients within a health system.
METHODS: The authors included 2 community cohorts (the MESA [Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis] Early HF study and the DHMS [Dallas Hearts and Minds Study]). Early HFpEF was defined by impaired exercise capacity or health-related quality of life with objective evidence of elevated cardiac filling pressures in patients without clinically diagnosed HF. The AI-HFpEF model was applied to resting echocardiograms, and the diagnostic performance was assessed. Multivariable models examined associations between AI-HFpEF output and early HFpEF phenotype. Separately, we included adults in the UTSW (University of Texas Southwestern) Health System with structurally normal echocardiograms and no prior HF (2018-2024) and assessed the association of AI-HFpEF output with incident HFpEF (adjudicated using a validated registry) using Cox regression.
RESULTS: In MESA (N = 2,544; 8.3% early HFpEF), AI-HFpEF outperformed H2FPEF for detecting early HFpEF (area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve [AUROC]: 0.77 vs 0.70). AI-HFpEF diagnostic positivity was associated with higher odds of early HFpEF (OR: 3.26; P < 0.001), lower 6-minute walk distance, and lower Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-12-Clinical Summary Score. Similarly, in DHMS (N = 624; 18.6% early HFpEF), AI-HFpEF outperformed H2FPEF (AUROC: 0.83 vs 0.77), and diagnostic positivity was associated with early HFpEF (OR: 6.76; P < 0.001), shorter exercise duration, and lower peak oxygen uptake. In the UTSW cohort (N = 6,876; median follow-up = 33 months; incident HFpEF = 3.4%), an AI-HFpEF diagnostic positive result was associated with >2-fold higher incident HFpEF risk (aHR: 2.08; P < 0.001). This association persisted across all conventional diastolic dysfunction grades.
CONCLUSIONS: AI-HFpEF identified the early HFpEF phenotype in community-dwelling adults and independently predicted incident clinical HFpEF among patients in a health system.

candidates.title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Pure Aortic Regurgitation: The Randomized SEASON-AR Clinical Trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: For patients with severe pure aortic regurgitation (AR) at high surgical risk, guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is often the only available option. Transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established treatment for aortic stenosis and has also been evaluated in patients with pure AR. However, no adequately powered randomized trial has compared TAVR with GDMT alone in this population.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective, investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial in China. Patients with severe pure AR for whom surgery was considered difficult or unacceptable by the local heart team or who persistently declined surgery were randomly assigned at a 1:1 ratio to receive transfemoral TAVR with the VitaFlow system plus GDMT or GDMT alone. The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year.
RESULTS: We assigned 210 patients with severe pure AR to the TAVR group (n=109) or GDMT group (n=101) at 18 centers. At 1-year follow-up, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the primary end point was significantly lower in the TAVR group than in the GDMT group (8.3% vs 24.8%; hazard ration [HR], 0.31 [95% CI, 0.14-0.66]; P=0.001), driven primarily by a reduction in heart failure rehospitalization (3.7% vs 21.3%; HR, 0.16 [95% CI, 0.06-0.47]; P < 0.001). TAVR was associated with higher rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation, most of which occurred within 30 days after the procedure.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with severe pure AR, TAVR plus GDMT significantly reduced the rate of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year compared with GDMT alone despite higher 30-day rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation.
